Utilities face substantial costs and planning for connecting data centers to expanding grids. AI drives power rethink Artificial intelligence is reshaping the energy demands of data centers, as computing equipment becomes more power-intensive and operators face a dual challenge of securing electricity while managing interactions between power supply, storage, cooling, and backup generation. U.S. data centers accounted for approximately 4.7% of the nation’s electricity consumption in 2024, a share projected to reach 11.8% by 2030 in Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory’s reference case. The International Energy Agency projected that a single advanced server rack could have peak power demand equivalent to that of 65 U.S. households by 2027. TransGrid Energy CEO Dr. Youngchoon Park said EnergyFluo “orchestrates grid, storage and on-site generation as one system and optimizes the load behind them, so operators can put more megawatts to work for IT and run their entire fleet from one intelligent view.” EnergyFluo was among the first AI-enabled products globally to receive certification from UL Solutions under UL 3115 in March 2026. Community trust becomes key 7x24 Exchange Chairman Bob Cassiliano said community opposition has overtaken several of the industry’s other longstanding concerns as the conference opened its technical program in San Antonio under the themeThe Intersection of AI & Traditional Data Centers. Cassiliano said, “Last year it was artificial intelligence, sustainability, the labor shortage,” and he added, “they have been superseded by community opposition to data centers.” AI futurist and former Google DeepMind executive Steve Brown told attendees, “We're using data centers to turn energy into intelligence,” as he described physical infrastructure required for an increasingly AI-driven economy. Brown said, “There may be a financial bubble, there may be a debt bubble, but I do not believe there is a demand bubble,” while he argued agentic computing could sustain expansion. Google power systems engineer Ashish Upreti and Cummins technical advisor Rich Scroggins described layered approaches to mitigating power swings, including software-level controls and supercapacitors for extremely short-duration spikes. Microgrids and grid costs Soaring demand from data center developers, widespread integration of clean power, and dwindling grid capacity on regional networks have spurred investment and development in microgrid solutions. The U.S. microgrid market is forecast to rise from $8 billion in 2025 to $21.2 billion by 2030, and a $2.6 billion acquisition in September of Utility Innovation Group by Vertiv was cited. Scale Microgrids General Manager of Data Centers Mike Grunow told Reuters Events that Scale is working on multiple new data center projects ranging from 200 to 500 MW, with several expected to exceed 1 GW. WTTW News said records filed by ComEd in an ongoing regulatory matter show that new infrastructure and system upgrades needed to connect 30 data centers to the grid will cost $3.1 billion. ComEd director of economic and workforce development Max Leichtman said, “The deposits that today stand at $721 million may continue to increase as these projects move forward and become more mature and more well-defined,” while consumer advocates warned ratepayers could face shortfalls.

artigo.texto: Russia’s Digital Development Ministry proposes placing strategically important data centers underground or in bunkers Russia’s Digital Development Ministry has approved recommendations for protecting data centers from drone attacks and other aerial threats, the Russian business daily Kommersant reported, citing a document it had reviewed. The ministry wants to divide critical data centers into three categories based on the consequences a potential attack could cause. The first category, K1, covers strategic facilities whose damage could disrupt key government functions for an hour or more. Security requirements will vary by category. For strategic facilities, the recommendations call for underground or bunker placement, Kommersant reported. The recommendations also call for reducing data centers’ visibility from the air, combining “physical reinforcement” with electronic warfare equipment and systems to counter aerial threats. The recommendations, which Kommersant reviewed, apply to data centers in Russia that are being designed, built, or already operating, regardless of ownership or operator. In October, Ukraine began striking similar facilities in Russia in response to Russian military strikes on data centers in Kyiv. Within a week, Ukrainian strikes hit three of the six data centers belonging to Yandex, in Sasovo in the Ryazan region, in Kaluga, and in Vladimir. Ukraine then struck a data center belonging to Sberbank in the Saratov region. IT market sources cited by Kommersant estimated that replacing equipment knocked out by the Ukrainian strikes on Yandex’s data centers will take up to six months. artigo.texto: Residents Question if Firefighters Can Handle Issues at Proposed Battery Storage Plant near Saugerties, NY SAUGERTIES, N.Y. — Councilperson Mike Ivino took issue with several people during a Town Board meeting after hearing remarks he considered to be an affront to his credibility on whether fires at a proposed Key Capture Energy lithium-ion battery facility could be properly contained. During the Wednesday, Oct. 21, session, Ivino said comments made by a couple — apparently between themselves — required him to respond with a forceful defense of the Centerville Fire District, which he oversees as chief. “I’m gonna bring you up to speed on the fire district that will oversee this project if it comes to fruition,” he said. “We are the best fire district in this town, OK? We have 60 members that provide service to the largest district in the town, OK?” Ivino questioned the couple, who left the meeting without identifying themselves, about where they live and then said they need to study details of the district. One of the two people said they felt the questions were inappropriate. “My question to you is: If you don’t live in the Centerville Fire District, I think you should start doing your homework on the fire districts that you might live in and see what their response times are, see what their membership is, what they respond to versus what we respond to,” he said. “I’m speaking to everybody, not just you,” Ivino added. “You kind of gave me a snide attitude when we were discussing or (a consultant) was discussing some facts about fire districts.” Key Capture Energy is seeking to construct a 100-megawatt lithium-ion energy storage system on 11 acres of a 59.8-acre parcel owned by KMP Realty Holdings adjacent to the village. The project continues to be controversial, with Ivino forcefully responding to criticism at several meetings since the 629-page application was filed last December. The Oct. 21 meeting included a discussion over how well the district could cover a battery fire. After mentioning that the Key Capture plan calls for 2.5 million gallons of water to be available at the site, Ivino said, “We’re not up here (on the Town Board) to be treated like a punching bag.” Resident Josepha Gutelius drew Ivino’s ire when she responded with statistics from the state Division of Homeland Security that stated that up to five million gallons of water would be needed for a major fire event at a lithium-ion battery facility. “That’s if every box is on fire and it’s catastrophic,” Ivino responded. “I recommend that you set up an appointment with me or one of my other officers and we can give you a rundown of … our equipment,” he said. After the meeting, resident Gaetana Ciarlante said Ivino’s approach to comments he perceived as adversarial was not reassuring. “We are not reassured that the current fire chief, who is also on the Town Board is taking a mature, unemotional, sensible look at this project, leaving many of us residents wondering why he is behaving in such a way,” she said. © 2026 Daily Freeman, Kingston, N.Y.. artigo.texto: Expansão dos data centers pode impulsionar o vanádio produzido na Bahia. Largo aposta em baterias e amplia negócios com a defesa dos Estados Unidos. A expansão dos data centers dedicados à inteligência artificial pode abrir novas oportunidades comerciais para o vanádio extraído na Bahia. A perspectiva é apresentada pela mineradora canadense Largo, responsável pela operação de Maracás Menchen, cujo co-CEO, Alberto Arias, identifica no crescimento da procura por baterias de armazenamento de energia nos Estados Unidos uma possibilidade de ampliar o mercado consumidor do mineral brasileiro. A movimentação ocorre em um momento de diversificação dos negócios da companhia. Além de acompanhar as necessidades energéticas dos centros de processamento de dados, a Largo já participa do fornecimento de vanádio destinado às reservas estratégicas americanas e começou a aproveitar outros minerais encontrados em sua operação baiana. Encomenda de US$ 60,1 milhões conecta vanádio brasileiro à defesa americana Uma das frentes comerciais da Largo envolve o abastecimento de materiais considerados estratégicos pelos Estados Unidos. Em julho, a mineradora recebeu um pedido inicial de US$ 60,1 milhões para fornecer pentóxido de vanádio de alta pureza, com entregas programadas até janeiro de 2030. - Mineração no Pará ganha relatório ESG com mais de 40 indicadores que abrangem 90% da produção mineral - STF restabelece suspensão da licença de instalação da Belo Sun para mina de ouro no Pará - R$ 180 milhões de dano ambiental: garimpeiros levavam o rejeito a laboratórios em Santaluz, na Bahia, onde o ouro era extraído com cianeto de sódio, e a PF faz nova operação no caso - Mineradora canadense amplia descoberta de terras raras em Minas Gerais, mas considera vender o projeto A encomenda veio depois de a empresa ter sido selecionada, em junho, como fornecedora da Agência de Logística de Defesa dos Estados Unidos (DLA). A iniciativa faz parte de um programa compartilhado de aquisições, com duração de cinco anos e limite financeiro de US$ 125 milhões. O produto extraído e processado na Bahia será incorporado aos estoques estratégicos americanos, podendo abastecer atividades industriais ligadas à fabricação de equipamentos de defesa e componentes aeronáuticos. Para Alberto Arias, esse interesse também está relacionado à intenção de países ocidentais de reduzir sua dependência de fornecedores como China e Rússia. O executivo defende maior reconhecimento do vanádio nas políticas voltadas aos minerais críticos, considerando sua importância para diferentes atividades industriais. Mineradora passa a aproveitar cobre e metais preciosos na Bahia A diversificação da Largo também ocorre dentro de Maracás Menchen. Desde agosto, a operação passou a recuperar um concentrado de cobre que reúne outros elementos de valor comercial, depois de obter autorização da Agência Nacional de Mineração (ANM). O processo utiliza materiais provenientes da própria atividade mineradora e permite recuperar, além do cobre, quantidades de ouro, prata, platina e paládio. Em vez de depender exclusivamente da produção de vanádio, a empresa começou a utilizar parte de sua estrutura industrial para transformar esses materiais em outro produto comercializável. A iniciativa faz parte da estratégia de melhorar o aproveitamento dos recursos minerais e a rentabilidade do empreendimento brasileiro. A mina fica a aproximadamente 250 quilômetros de Salvador e iniciou suas atividades produtivas em 2014. Explorada a céu aberto, possui um dos depósitos de vanádio de maior teor do mundo e representa o principal ativo da companhia canadense, que tem ações negociadas nas bolsas de Toronto e Nova York. Baterias de fluxo colocam vanádio no caminho da inteligência artificial Embora tenha aplicações tradicionais na produção de aços resistentes e ligas metálicas especiais, o vanádio passou a despertar interesse por outra característica: sua utilização em tecnologias capazes de armazenar eletricidade durante várias horas. É nesse mercado que a Largo pretende ampliar sua presença. Em 2025, a mineradora se associou à americana Stryten Energy para criar a Storion Energy, dedicada ao desenvolvimento de componentes e eletrólitos para baterias de fluxo de vanádio. Nesses equipamentos, a energia é armazenada por meio de soluções líquidas contendo o mineral, movimentadas entre reservatórios e células eletroquímicas. O funcionamento difere daquele encontrado nas baterias convencionais de íons de lítio. Entre as vantagens dessa tecnologia estão a capacidade de manter reservas de eletricidade por períodos prolongados, a durabilidade dos sistemas e o menor risco de incêndio. Essas características permitem considerar seu uso em redes de distribuição de energia, estabelecimentos industriais e instalações que dependem de alimentação elétrica contínua. Segundo Arias, a empresa formada com a parceira americana vem registrando, nos últimos dois anos, um crescimento expressivo da demanda por baterias de vanádio destinadas à indústria de data centers. Crescimento dos data centers pode estimular produção de vanádio no Brasil A necessidade de manter servidores e equipamentos de processamento em operação contínua torna o armazenamento de eletricidade uma questão importante para os novos empreendimentos de inteligência artificial. Com o avanço dessas instalações, também aumenta a necessidade de investimentos em infraestrutura de geração, transmissão e reserva energética. Para a Largo, parte dessa expansão poderá representar um mercado adicional para o vanádio, hoje amplamente utilizado pela siderurgia. Alberto Arias relatou que convidou representantes da parceira americana para conhecer a operação brasileira. Segundo o executivo, o potencial de ampliação da capacidade produtiva da mina baiana impressionou os representantes da empresa. O interesse não está limitado aos Estados Unidos. A expectativa da mineradora é que o desenvolvimento de novos data centers em território brasileiro também possa favore

artigo.texto: The Cap Times is an independent newsroom serving Madison and Wisconsin. Sign up for the Morning Update to receive news in your inbox each morning. As employees and students grapple with questions around artificial intelligence, the University of Wisconsin-Madison has decided to work with a Milwaukee company for some of its data center needs. For years, the university has previously relied on two data center services to host research and administrative computing for campus, according to Rob Cramer, UW-Madison’s top financial official. One is run by the state Department of Administration, and the other is run by a private company, US Signal. With UW-Madison’s contract with US Signal scheduled to end in early 2029, Cramer recently told the UW system’s Board of Regents, the university began looking for a replacement provider. After a bid process, UW-Madison selected Milwaukee-based Data Holdings. “This will provide us with a long-term solution that will both meet research computing needs and provide, basically, a backup for our administrative computing,” Cramer told the Board of Regents this summer. “It increases our capacity and it also moves us forward with respect to some of the higher demands of current research computing, including liquid cooling of the equipment.” The switch will also improve the university’s ability to secure new grants and contracts, according to the board’s meeting materials. Board of Regents members approved the switch in August. The transition will cost about $17 million and be funded by UW-Madison. Cramer estimated the total cost over the next decade will be about $60 million. Data Holdings is owned by the Forest County Potawatomi Community tribe in northern Wisconsin, as a subsidiary company of Potawatomi Ventures. The company’s customers include government, healthcare, hospitality and other organizations, according to Ryan Brooks, Data Holdings’ chief technology officer and general manager. “The Tribe's long-term perspective and commitment to responsible and sustainable investment helped shape the development of Data Holdings from the beginning and continues to influence how we operate and grow today,” Brooks told the Cap Times in an email. Increased development of data centers and how to regulate the facilities has prompted debate in communities across Wisconsin and the nation, and percolated in the state’s fall elections, including in the gubernatorial race. Data Holdings opened a two-story, 46,000-square-foot facility in Milwaukee in 2013. The scale of the building pales in comparison to some larger proposed data centers in Wisconsin, such as Meta’s facility in Beaver Dam, which is expected to span more than 500 acres. At a campus meeting this month, faculty leaders asked interim Chancellor Eric Wilcots where the university stood on data centers. “We're not going to take a position on large data centers across the state. That is not our place,” Wilcots said. “Can we inform the debate and the discussion? Absolutely. … Because we have experts who think about energy policy. We have experts who think about fresh water. … We have experts who think about the role of people in government.” In addition to contracts with data center providers, UW-Madison operates its own data centers on campus for specific research and administrative needs, said Greg Bump, a university spokesperson. “There are small facilities within the Computer Sciences and Statistics building serving the Division of Information Technology, College of Computing and Artificial Intelligence, Wisconsin Public Radio, and others,” Bump said in an email to the Cap Times. “Across the street, the Atmospheric, Oceanic and Space Sciences building has its own small data center serving the department and processing satellite data and creating weather models used all over the world.” Data centers can vary in scale, from the size of a closet to the size of a warehouse, according to Kyle Cranmer, a physics professor and director of UW-Madison’s Data Science Institute. Some research projects at the university collect lots of data, he said. It may make sense to store and process the data locally, out of convenience and to allow more local control. Depending on the need, though, it may be more cost effective and energy efficient to centralize resources at a data center, he said. UW-Madison has been working to scale up its artificial intelligence-related research, such as through its RISE-AI initiative and new College of Computing and Artificial Intelligence. “AI is not just about chatbots, like ChatGPT,” Cranmer said. “There's lots of other kinds of artificial intelligence that ... can be more relevant for science problems.” For instance, researchers are working to find ways to remove toxic “forever chemicals” known as PFAS from water, he said, and to make society more resilient to convective storms that produce tornadoes and hail. Generally, Cranmer added, “AI is definitely driving a lot of the increase in demand for data centers,” but not all AI requires big data centers. UW-Madison administrators designated 2026 as the university’s “Year of AI Readiness and Competency.” Members of a working group have wrestled with questions about how to think about and use AI on campus, Wilcots said. “What kind of guidance can we give to instructors? But also how we're going to think about using it administratively,” he said. “Because there's a lot of things I think in the AI space where we will be using it. We are using it. But we've got to think about how to do that carefully. We've got to think about issues of data privacy. artigo.texto: Europe is accelerating the launch of new auctions linked to energy storage , with Portugal and Italy making progress in their respective competitive procedures during October. While the Portuguese government will auction 1,050 MVA of grid access capacity and the Italian operator Terna opens registrations for its 2028 capacity market, Spain is still awaiting the first calls for its own mechanism. These moves come against a backdrop of growing need for flexibility, reliability, and the integration of renewable energy into European electricity systems. However, the instruments differ: Portugal will allocate grid access rights for storage projects, while Italy will remunerate available capacity to ensure security of supply. In the Spanish case, the approval of Order TED/966/2026 , published on September 17 in the Official State Gazette (BOE), finally establishes the regulatory framework for its capacity market. However, this regulation still needs to be translated into the auctions that will define the contracting conditions for companies in the sector. Portugal to tender 1 GW for batteries: access conditions and operational restrictions On October 22nd, the Government of Portugal formalized the opening of two competitive procedures for a maximum of 1,050 MVA , aimed at facilitating the incorporation of storage systems through the allocation of reserve titles for injection capacity into the electricity grid. The tenders were approved through provisions 12924-B/2026 and 12924-C/2026 , published in the Diário da República, and will be managed by the General Directorate of Energy and Geology (DGEG). Of the total volume, 750 MVA correspond to independent storage facilities, known as standalone , while the remaining 300 MVA will be reserved for renewable generation centers with batteries located on the same site. Both procedures will be carried out through electronic auctions, with capacity distributed among the connection points established in the documentation of each call. The initiative opens up new possibilities for battery developers, although the allocation of injection capacity does not guarantee having an equivalent power to charge energy from the grid . In this regard, access limits for demand are a determining factor for project operation. Load capacity will depend on the conditions of each node, with particularly relevant restrictions in certain locations, such as Sines, according to sector information published by Optimize Energy. Furthermore, the shared technical terms regarding the upcoming tenders contemplate the possibility that the network operator may limit the operation of storage systems during certain periods of the year. Specifically, the industry documentation indicates up to 500 hours per year of combined charging and discharging restrictions for stand-alone batteries and up to 750 hours of grid charging restrictions for hybrid projects . These limits should be verified against the final specifications applicable to each installation. Therefore, the allocated capacity does not necessarily imply unrestricted availability for all 8,760 hours of the year. For developers, access conditions, location, and operational limitations must be incorporated into the technical design and economic model. This aspect is especially relevant for projects that depend on energy arbitrage, whose profitability is linked to the possibility of charging electricity during periods of reduced prices and unloading during the hours of highest market value . Italy opens its call for proposals for 2028 and reduces the recognized power output of batteries. For its part, Terna, the Italian operator, confirmed that the main auction of the capacity market for the 2028 delivery period will be held on December 21, 2026 , starting at 10:00 a.m. The operator opened the application period on October 20 , while interested companies will have until November 3, at 12:00 pm , to submit their applications. Subsequently, the schedule sets November 23 as the deadline for incorporating certain technical documentation and completing specific guarantees, while December 14 will be the deadline for submitting the deposits corresponding to the participation. The call is accompanied by modifications to the power accreditation coefficients for storage systems , known as derating factors, which determine what proportion of the installed power is recognized as firm capacity within the mechanism. The new technical provisions were approved on October 16 by the Ministry of Environment and Energy Security , following the regulatory review by the Energy, Networks and Environment Regulatory Authority (ARERA). The change particularly affects four-hour battery projects, whose recognized power decreases in all Italian electric zones, although with significant differences depending on the location. In the North and North Central regions , the coefficient falls from 51% to 40%, while in the South Central region it drops from 54% to 51%. The largest reductions are in the South and Calabria, where the percentage falls from 40% to 21% , and in Sicily and Sardinia, with a reduction from 31% to 21%. In practical terms, a 100 MW battery with four hours of storage will be able to provide 40 MW of capacity in the North, 51 MW in the Central South and only 21 MW in the South, Calabria, Sicily and Sardinia. This means that, for an installation located in the South and Calabria, the recognized power is reduced by 47.5% compared to the previous parameters , which directly modifies the volume of capacity that it will be able to offer in the auction. The revision responds to the increased forecasts for the integration of batteries into the Italian electricity system. A greater presence of storage capacity modifies the contribution of each additional installation to meeting peak demand periods. artigo.texto: NASSAU COUNTY, Fla. – Nassau County’s Fact-Finding Committee on Data Center Development has published an initial draft report outlining possible rules for data centers, as the county continues a temporary, yearlong moratorium meant to give leaders time to study impacts and consider new regulations. Monday’s workshop — the first of two public workshops on the draft — drew residents who urged county leaders to slow down, tighten guardrails, and in some cases, stop data centers entirely. Residents: “Err on the side of caution” During public comment, residents questioned whether data centers would bring enough benefit to outweigh potential impacts. One speaker told county leaders, “I don’t think that we should be opening our doors to data centers at all.” Another asked officials to tighten oversight, saying: “I would ask you to err on the side of caution, a little more regulation, more protection.” Others asked county leaders to put the issue directly to voters: “Put it to a vote for the people.” What the draft report recommends County documents describe data centers as facilities that support essential services — including communications, health care and government operations — but the draft also acknowledges concerns raised in public workshops, including water use, power demand, land use compatibility and long-term accountability. Among the key recommendations in the draft report: - Create a clear framework to classify data centers by type and scale, and spell out where each classification may be allowed under Nassau County zoning and Future Land Use rules. - Strengthen the development review process and transparency, including coordination with other agencies and limiting nondisclosure agreements that restrict information needed for public accountability. - Protect water resources and ensure utility and infrastructure capacity, including project-specific assessments and operational reporting on water and power use. - Set enforceable design and mitigation standards for impacts such as lighting and sound, including measurable standards and buffers/setbacks. - Require monitoring, compliance and decommissioning plans to address long-term operations, changing technology and closure. - Revisit economic incentives, including a recommendation that Nassau County remove data centers as a “target industry,” making them ineligible for certain county economic development incentives. The ban question — and the county attorney’s warning As residents pressed for stricter rules, the conversation also turned to whether Nassau County could simply ban data centers outright. “Tell me, convince me, convince all of us, what is the benefit to this community?” one resident said. During the workshop, Commissioner John F. Martin asked: “Why can’t we just ban them?” County Attorney Denise May responded that a ban could create legal exposure, saying, “My opinion that an outright ban is not only risky but goes against what the statute calls for which is for your absolute comprehensive planning.” Commissioners discussed pursuing tougher regulations that would hold up legally — including larger setbacks. “Maybe we overshoot all requirements but I also believe you can’t regulate it out of existence,” Commissioner A.M. “Hupp” Huppmann said. What happens next Nassau County officials say the draft report will continue to be refined with public input. - Second workshop: Nov. 9 - Final report expected: Nov. 25 - Potential BOCC vote on regulations: Jan. 25, 2027 Residents can track the schedule and read the draft report through Nassau County’s data center webpage and through updates on News4JAX.com.

artigo.texto: {KXLG, Watertown, SD} Area residents will have an opportunity this week to learn more about a major commercial energy storage project proposed for the region. The Local Review Committee (LRC), established by the South Dakota Public Utilities Commission, will host a public informational meeting regarding Crowned Ridge Energy Storage I, LLC’s proposed Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project. The meeting is scheduled for Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. at the First District Association of Local Governments Office, located at 418 18th Avenue NE in Watertown. The session is free and open to all members of the public. During the meeting, committee members will receive a preliminary report on a required Social and Economic Effect/Impact Study. This evaluation assesses how the addition of large-scale energy storage infrastructure could impact local public services, tax revenues, employment, and community resources throughout the area. Members of the public are encouraged to attend to review the preliminary findings and learn more about the proposed development. The committee appointed by the South Dakota Public Utilities Commission to review the project includes Codington County Commission Chair Troy VanDusen, Grant County Commission Chair William Tostenson, City of South Shore Mayor Jamie Dolen, Waverly 14-5 School District Board President Penny Thyen, and Milbank 25-4 School District Board President Richard Schwandt.

artigo.texto: Fulton County residents weigh draft data center rules, call for bigger setbacks FULTON COUNTY, Ind. (WSBT) — People in Fulton County are weighing in on proposed rules for future data centers. The Area Plan Commission presented a draft of its Data Center Development Standards, and residents are already calling for changes. Board members stressed that the meeting was a discussion, not a public hearing. They walked residents through the draft and invited feedback as they consider what rules should govern future data center development. The nine-page draft outlines standards developers would have to meet to build a data center in Fulton County. Residents focused on two key issues: how far a facility must be from sensitive locations and how the county measures its size. The draft would require large or hyperscale data centers to be at least 1,500 feet from churches, schools, hospitals and nursing homes. Some residents said that distance should be greater, citing concerns about noise. “It does need to be a larger setback from a church, school or hospital. I would agree in general that you probably are going to want to push the setback requirements a little bit longer from that. And that reason is honestly due to the noise,” one Fulton County resident said. Residents also questioned the draft’s use of megawatts to determine permit requirements. They suggested using square footage instead, saying it would make it easier to understand how much land a facility could occupy and how it could affect farmland and natural resources. “When we're talking about property, use of property, natural resources, how much farmland is going to this, if we're dealing in square foot it's a lot easier to conceptualize and see than it is in megawatts,” a resident said. Another resident questioned why the standards could not use square footage to make the rules easier for the public to understand. “Why isn't it just simplified by square footage? That would make it very easy for the common person to understand. I don't know what a megawatt takes up space,” the resident said. The draft ordinance also addresses noise, water management, energy efficiency and financial assurances for decommissioning a facility. The commission is gathering feedback as it considers the proposed standards for future data center development in Fulton County.

artigo.texto: Longer drone flights, full-shift humanoid robots, lighter and faster race cars, and data centers that don't burden the grid. IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Engineers building drones, humanoid robots, race cars, data center power systems, and electric aircraft want more energy in less weight and space, plus the power to use it. Enevate Technologies today introduced Trifecta, a licensable cell technology designed so they no longer have to choose between energy density, power, and cycle life. Battery engineers live by an unwritten rule: energy, power, or cycle life, pick two. At the cutting edge, they often get just one, paying for it with oversized packs, shorter missions, and lost payload. Trifecta designs match or exceed the energy density of leading lithium-metal and solid-state cells without their usual safety and charge-rate problems, and long-life configurations reach 1,000 cycles. "Engineers have spent years designing around their batteries," said Benjamin Park, CEO of Enevate Technologies. "Trifecta flips that. We want to have open conversations about how our technology can change how you design things." Trifecta comes in five modeled configurations: Figures are for modeled designs that build on a successful proof of concept with earlier prototype cells. Enevate Technologies works with each customer to match or tailor a configuration, then helps get cells built by a licensee, through a custom build, or by the customer's existing supplier. Battery manufacturers interested in licensing Trifecta to produce cells for their own customers are invited to reach out. To book a technical briefing or discuss licensing, email [email protected]. About Enevate Technologies Enevate Technologies develops and licenses high-energy, high-power battery cell technology. It builds on technology and team members from Enevate Corporation, whose 20 years of battery innovation was validated by global automakers and cell manufacturers and produced more than 700 patents issued and pending. Its open, cooperative culture gives customers a direct path to its experts. Learn more at enevate.com. artigo.texto: Projeto de inteligência artificial prevê usar energia hidrelétrica no Paraguai, com primeira fase em 2027 e possibilidade de expansão para cerca de 280 MW, enquanto Brasil não participou da agenda em Itaipu. O governo dos Estados Unidos anunciou uma parceria entre a americana Crusoe e a paraguaia Araico para desenvolver uma infraestrutura de computação de alto desempenho e inteligência artificial no Paraguai, abastecida por energia hidrelétrica associada a Itaipu. O acordo foi apresentado durante a visita do vice-secretário de Estado americano Christopher Landau ao país, em outubro de 2026, mas a agenda realizada na usina não contou com representantes da Diretoria Brasileira de Itaipu nem do governo brasileiro. Segundo o UOL, a visita de Landau à hidrelétrica ocorreu em 21 de outubro, ao lado do presidente paraguaio Santiago Peña e do diretor-geral paraguaio de Itaipu, Justo Zacarías Irún. - Rio Grande do Norte libera instalação de planta que prevê 200 mil toneladas de amônia verde por ano usando energia 100% renovável - Mato Grosso do Sul coloca quase 2 milhões de painéis solares em operação após investimento de R$ 3 bilhões em dois complexos solares - Brasil se junta a 23 países para transformar ondas e marés em eletricidade e desenvolver 4 tecnologias de energia oceânica - Mercado de energia solar vê investimentos associados a painéis caírem R$ 15,8 bilhões e demanda por equipamentos despenca 48% no Brasil A binacional informou ao portal que a programação foi organizada pelo governo do Paraguai e pela margem paraguaia da empresa. A ausência brasileira, porém, não significa que o Paraguai tenha utilizado a parcela de energia pertencente ao Brasil. Itaipu esclareceu que, pelo tratado binacional, cada país tem direito a 50% da energia produzida e administra sua demanda nacional por meio das entidades responsáveis em cada lado da fronteira. Projeto de IA pode chegar a cerca de 280 MW O anúncio envolve a Crusoe, empresa americana especializada em infraestrutura computacional para inteligência artificial e serviços de nuvem, e a Araico, desenvolvedora paraguaia de energia e infraestrutura. De acordo com a Crusoe, o projeto será sua primeira implantação dedicada de AI Cloud na América Latina. A primeira etapa está prevista para entrar em operação em meados de 2027, com possibilidade de alcançar 106 MW de capacidade de tecnologia da informação e opções de expansão de longo prazo para aproximadamente 280 MW. A companhia afirma que a instalação ficará próxima à infraestrutura elétrica de Itaipu e utilizará a disponibilidade de geração hidrelétrica paraguaia para atender clientes americanos e empresas da América Latina. A Araico ficará responsável pelo desenvolvimento local e pela infraestrutura do terreno, enquanto a Crusoe deverá administrar a operação computacional e fornecer a capacidade física utilizada pela plataforma Crusoe Cloud. O vice-secretário Christopher Landau afirmou que o empreendimento tem potencial para se tornar um dos maiores investimentos privados estrangeiros da história paraguaia. O valor definitivo da parceria, entretanto, não foi divulgado oficialmente pela Crusoe e pela Araico. Cifras maiores já foram mencionadas publicamente por representantes envolvidos no projeto. O jornal paraguaio ABC Color informou que Alejandro Zuccolillo, executivo da Araico, chegou a citar um plano de até US$ 12 bilhões em três anos, com uma primeira fase estimada em aproximadamente US$ 300 milhões. Esses valores, porém, não constam do comunicado oficial da Crusoe e não devem ser tratados como investimento já contratado pela empresa americana. Contrato de energia amplia escala do projeto A questão do fornecimento de energia ganhou novos detalhes depois do anúncio. Em 23 de outubro, a Administração Nacional de Eletricidade do Paraguai, a ANDE, anunciou a assinatura de um contrato de fornecimento por 15 anos com a empresa Kuntur S.A., prevendo consumo crescente até 286 MW. A estatal informou que o fornecimento começará em 1º de dezembro de 2026, inicialmente com 6 MW, e poderá alcançar o limite contratado em abril de 2029. Segundo o ABC Color, a Kuntur está vinculada à Araico. O presidente da ANDE afirmou ao jornal que a empresa possui estrutura societária ligada ao grupo envolvido no projeto de inteligência artificial. Ainda assim, os comunicados oficiais da ANDE e da Crusoe não apresentam de forma inequívoca todos esses documentos como partes do mesmo contrato empresarial. Por isso, as relações entre Crusoe, Araico e Kuntur precisam ser tratadas separadamente enquanto não houver documentação pública mais detalhada. O contrato anunciado pela ANDE estabelece tarifa média de US$ 56,39 por MWh na fase inicial, em 23 kV, e de US$ 48,91 por MWh quando o fornecimento passar para 220 kV. As obras necessárias para a conexão na Subestação Yguazú deverão ser financiadas pela própria empresa contratante. Os números são próximos da escala de longo prazo apresentada pela Crusoe, que menciona aproximadamente 280 MW, mas existe uma diferença nas descrições de localização. Enquanto a empresa americana afirma que sua instalação ficará próxima à infraestrutura de Itaipu, o contrato divulgado pela ANDE cita a Subestação Yguazú. Sem detalhamento adicional, não é seguro tratar os dois documentos como perfeitamente equivalentes. Energia de Itaipu vira ativo para atrair data centers O interesse do Paraguai em data centers está diretamente ligado à disponibilidade de energia hidrelétrica. Itaipu possui 14 GW de potência instalada, distribuídos entre 20 unidades geradoras, e é administrada conjuntamente por Brasil e Paraguai. A produção é repartida entre os dois países conforme o Tratado de Itaipu. Historicamente, como o Paraguai consome menos do que sua metade em diversos períodos, parte do excedente paraguaio é aproveitada pelo sistema brasileiro de acordo com as regras do acordo binacional. A atração de grandes consumidores no lado paraguaio pode aumentar o uso doméstico da parcela de energia a que o país já tem dire

artigo.texto: Nio Taps EVE and Gotion for Trial Cell Batch as Firefly Owners Get a 17,000-Yuan Range Boost Published on 10/26/2026 at 14:21 | Editorial boerse-global.de Nio's in-house battery ambitions are edging toward the factory floor, but the company's more immediate commercial news is coming from its smallest model. Reports from battery-industry outlet Jipian Lab indicate that EVE Energy and Gotion High-Tech have been lined up to build a very small initial batch of Nio's own cylindrical cells, with volume production unlikely any time soon. The work remains in sampling, testing and pilot-manufacturing territory — a validation hurdle that makes a rapid jump to larger volumes difficult. That distinction matters. Nio develops the large-format cells internally and outsources the manufacturing, a route that differs from its earlier plan to build its own plant in Hefei, where equipment purchases were reportedly halted. The first cell version was unveiled in December 2023 with an energy density of 292 Wh/kg and 5C fast-charging capability — figures that describe the state of development at the time. The cell format has since moved beyond that original design, so the announced small series cannot simply be equated with the concept first presented. No Launch Date for the 120 kWh Pack The planned 120 kWh battery still has no start date. CEO William Li said on 7 August that development would continue, and the ET9 instead reached the market in December 2024 with a CATL battery. A successful first batch would therefore not signal an imminent launch for the planned pack, and no timetable for scaling production has been given. Li put spending on battery development at more than 2 billion yuan in September, underlining the project's weight for Nio without yet demonstrating a financial return. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Nio? CATL remains central in parallel. Nio is expanding its intake of prismatic CATL cells for Onvo and Firefly, so internal development and external supply run side by side — the expected trial production does not replace those relationships. Firefly Gains a Bigger Battery — at a Price On the product side, Firefly added a battery option on Friday that lifts its stated CLTC range from 420 to 560 kilometres. Existing owners can upgrade too, at a cost of 17,000 yuan. The offer is thus not confined to new buyers, though the range figure is a CLTC measure and should be read as such rather than as a promise for every driving situation. Firefly had already passed 90,000 cumulative deliveries on 16 October, giving the new option an established customer base to work with. How many owners will pay for the upgrade cannot be inferred from the launch alone. Deliveries provided the operating backdrop. Nio reported handover of the 160,000th third-generation ES8 in Xi'an on Friday — a model-specific milestone distinct from group-wide volume. On 17 October, president Qin Lihong cited Wilson data showing 111,638 retail sales across the three brands in China in the third quarter of 2026, ahead of BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Audi combined. That comparison is a China-market ranking, not a global one, and not a measure of the Nio brand alone. Concrete Steps Versus a Feasibility Study Beyond its current lineup, Nio is weighing further options. A Wednesday report said the company is examining the feasibility of vehicle assembly in Thailand, with no investment decision taken. The contrast in certainty is stark: the Firefly battery option and the delivery milestones are completed operational events, while Thai assembly remains under review. For investors, product offering and vehicle sales are the firmer anchors for now — and on the battery front, the naming of manufacturing partners makes the production path more concrete, even as the move to high-volume output and the launch of the planned vehicle pack stay unresolved. artigo.texto: Environment Minister Dr. Tamara El Zein launched preparations for Lebanon’s national carbon market roadmap, supported by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and its Climate Promise initiative, under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. El Zein said the initiative aims to transform emissions reductions into financing and investment opportunities, particularly through internationally recognized carbon credits. Chairing a technical meeting with international expert Dr. Axel Michaelowa and officials concerned with solid waste management, she outlined opportunities for developing eligible projects in the waste sector. She stressed that carbon financing could improve project viability, attract investment and support sustainable environmental solutions. El Zein announced plans to expand consultations to other sectors, particularly energy, in coordination with relevant ministries. She emphasized that carbon credits require rigorous measurement, verification and compliance with international standards, reaffirming that climate financing must deliver tangible environmental and economic benefits.

artigo.texto: Have CATL's fundamentals changed? CATL has found itself in a rather delicate situation recently. Recently, CATL released its 2026 Q3 financial report, with both revenue and profit continuing to grow. In the first three quarters of this year, its daily net profit exceeded 230 million yuan, showing an astonishing cash absorption capacity. However, the day after the financial report was released, CATL's intraday drop once exceeded 10%. Prior to that, its stock price had fallen for consecutive months, dropping from the historical intraday high of 467.35 yuan in May to 227.9 yuan as of the writing date, which was almost cut in half. The biggest concern of the market is the "de-CATL trend". Automakers hope to reduce their dependence on CATL, and second-tier battery manufacturers hope to seize more orders. Since September, a number of new energy vehicle makers including Li Auto, XPeng, Xiaomi and Leapmotor have officially announced their self-developed battery progress one after another, and reached closer cooperation with second-tier battery manufacturers such as CALB, Sunwoda and Honeycomb Energy. CATL still leads the industry, but the market is worried about its future and has begun to vote with its feet. When the era dividend of power batteries fades away, where will CATL's next "era" start? 01 Warning lights on performance In the third quarter, CATL delivered a mixed report card. The good news is that CATL's revenue scale is still incredibly strong. In the first three quarters of 2026, CATL achieved a revenue of 442.137 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 56.19%; the net profit attributable to shareholders reached 64.53 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 31.6%. Among them, the revenue in the third quarter reached 165.221 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 58.58%, hitting a record high; the net profit attributable to shareholders was 21.246 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 14.54%. The concern is that while CATL's revenue is rising, its profit has not kept pace. From the first to the third quarter of this year, CATL's single-quarter revenue growth rates were 52.46%, 56.9% and 58.58% respectively; however, its net profit growth rate kept sliding, reaching 48.55%, 36.4% and 14.54% respectively. The scissors gap between the company's revenue and profit growth rate has expanded from less than 4 percentage points in the first quarter to more than 44 percentage points in the third quarter. The company's comprehensive gross profit margin also dropped all the way from 24.82% in the first quarter to 20.69% in the third quarter, and the pressure on the cost side is clearly visible. Policy changes are the most direct influencing factor. Starting from September 1, 2026, the consumption tax on lithium batteries has been levied, with a current tax rate of 2%, and it will be levied at 4% from September 2027; the export tax rebate for batteries has been reduced from 9% to 6% since April 1, 2026, and will be completely cancelled from January 2027. However, the current automobile price war has reached a white-hot stage. According to data from the China Automobile Dealers Association, from January to August this year, the revenue of the automobile industry was 7.0062 trillion yuan, with a year-on-year increase of only 2.9%, while the profit dropped by 16% year-on-year. Against this background, it is difficult for CATL to fully pass on this part of the tax cost to downstream automakers, and it may even encounter reverse price pressure from automakers on battery costs due to profit contraction. External pressure is also reshaping CATL's product structure. The domestic automobile market is under pressure, and the energy storage business has become the main incremental driver. CATL disclosed that the total sales of power and energy storage batteries in the third quarter exceeded 260 GWh, with energy storage accounting for about a quarter, and the sales growth rate was close to 60%, far higher than that of power batteries. However, although the gross profit margin of CATL's energy storage business is slightly higher than that of power batteries, it is a business with low unit price, long service cycle and low profit elasticity. In the long run, its marginal contribution to profit is far lower than that of power batteries of the same volume. The sharp drop in lithium carbonate prices is also impacting the selling price of power batteries. Since May this year, the spot price of lithium carbonate has dropped by more than 40% cumulatively, and the battery cost has decreased. However, the drop in lithium price has led to a reduction in battery selling price, and the profit difference may not remain in the company's accounts, and may even reduce customers' stocking expectation in the fourth quarter. In addition, CATL is also actively "increasing costs". In the third quarter, in response to industry initiatives, the company voluntarily shortened the upstream account period and increased prepayments, resulting in a 47.78% year-on-year increase in accounts receivable compared with the beginning of the year, and the inventory reached a record high of 144.77 billion yuan. Under internal and external pressures, although CATL sold more batteries, it barely made more money. In response, CATL said that it is mainly affected by short-term product changes and tax policies, and does not represent the long-term direction. However, the capital market may not hold the same view. 02 The truth of the "de-CATL trend" As early as a few months ago, the capital market had already cast a "bearish vote" on CATL — "de-CATL" has changed from a slogan to a collective action of some brands. In 2022, Zeng Qinghong, Chairman of GAC Group, said "I am working for CATL", which uncovered the undercurrent between automakers and CATL: power batteries account for 40%-60% of the total vehicle cost. artigo.texto: Huawei's foray into the battery swapping industry has made NIO absolutely thrilled. NIO is no longer the "lone warrior in battery swapping" at last. On October 19, Zhiyue signed a strategic cooperation agreement on smart battery swapping ecosystem with CATL and E-Car Service, where the three parties will connect vehicles, battery swapping stations and the cloud, to promote the synergy between Huawei Qiankun and CATL's Choco-Swap network. Two points are particularly emphasized in the cooperation: First, to create a "smart and non-inductive energy replenishment" experience, where vehicles will realize a full-process intelligent closed loop of autonomously judging energy replenishment demands, searching for stations, entering stations, aligning positions, completing 99-second full-automatic battery swapping, and driving away independently. Second, Zhiyue will officially join CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem, and work with strategic partners to jointly expand the battery swapping energy replenishment ecosystem around the adaptation and access of cooperative models to CATL's Choco-Swap network. In simple terms, the cooperation essentially leverages Huawei's intelligent driving capabilities, and with the help of CATL's battery swapping network, the intelligent driving system will independently decide "whether to swap the battery" and "where to swap the battery", so as to realize the smart and non-inductive energy replenishment experience. On the premise that the technology is fully verified, the relevant brands under Zhiyue including the Jing series will further launch battery swapping models. It is rumored that CATL and Zhiyue are advancing the development of the first batch of five battery swapping models, which are scheduled to be launched in 2027. Coincidentally, on October 22, BAIC Group also officially announced that it has signed a "million-unit" battery swapping strategic cooperation agreement with CATL. According to the agreement, BAIC Group will promote the access of adapted models of its multiple brands to CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem, and strive for the target of one million battery swapping vehicles. It is worth noting that BAIC Group will also open its dealer network resources, while CATL's Choco-Swap will accelerate the station deployment relying on dealer stores, and the two sides will jointly explore the joint operation model. Although the battery swapping models of Huawei and BAIC, as well as their specific launch time, have not been officially confirmed, this series of "alliances and collaborations" has indeed brought a new trend: in the pure electric vehicle market, flash charging and ultra-fast charging are not the only solutions, and battery swapping is gaining recognition from more industrial players. What NIO has been waiting for is not just Huawei's entry When talking about battery swapping, NIO is an unavoidable name. Since its establishment more than ten years ago, NIO has always taken its battery swapping system capability as its "moat". However, battery swapping is a capital-intensive business, which requires investment in construction, maintenance and battery reserve. If it only relies on its own vehicle models, the scale and utilization rate of the battery swapping network will eventually be limited by sales volume. Therefore, from the very beginning, NIO has hoped that more players will join the big family of battery swapping. From another perspective, on the same track of battery swapping, NIO's experience in battery swapping can also be transformed into real competitive advantages. In fact, since November 2023, NIO has reached battery swapping cooperation with Changan Automobile, Geely Holding Group, Chery Automobile, JAC Group, Lotus, GAC Group, FAW Group and other enterprises. However, these "cooperation frameworks" are far less significant than the cooperation finalized between NIO and Geely. On September 28, NIO and Geely Holding reached a comprehensive strategic cooperation in the field of charging and battery swapping. According to the agreement, Geely will take a stake in NIO Energy with the equity of Yiyi Internet and cash, holding 30% of the shares after the transaction is completed; Geely will develop consumer-oriented battery swapping models, with NIO Energy providing battery swapping services. The fact that multiple battery swapping cooperations have been reached in the industry in a short period of time is by no means "child's play", but indicates that in the mainstream passenger vehicle market in the future, battery swapping models will no longer be exclusive to NIO. Geely, Huawei's Jing series brand will all launch competitive products in this field. From a competitive perspective, NIO has more rivals now, which may affect the sales of its own products. But for NIO, its first-mover advantage in battery swapping is still solid. What's more, the completion of a battery swapping station does not mean that the battery swapping business is successful. The bigger "hurdle" lies in operation. A battery swapping station needs a sufficient number of vehicles in continuous use to spread the costs of equipment, site, battery reserve and operation personnel. Car owners hope to have more stations nearby, while operators hope to get more orders from each station. The two sides restrict each other, which makes battery swapping easily fall into a vicious circle: the network is not large enough for users to choose battery swapping; without enough users, the network cannot continue to expand. This is also the reason why NIO keeps looking for partners. However, it must be made clear that as more participants join the battery swapping industry, whether the energy replenishment networks can be interconnected and whether the standards can be compatible is still a practical problem to be solved. artigo.texto: Supercharging is getting faster and faster. Why are car manufacturers setting their sights on battery swapping? In China's new energy vehicle industry, battery swapping has long been a niche route, but now this solution has suddenly become the focus of major industry players. On October 19, 2026, Huawei HiChord, CATL and E-Chen New Energy signed the "Strategic Cooperation Agreement for Intelligent Energy Replenishment Ecosystem". The three parties will strengthen cooperation in swappable batteries and battery swapping networks, and work with ecosystem partners to jointly build an intelligent battery swapping ecosystem. In the future, battery-swapping models equipped with Huawei's intelligent driving solution will support autonomous battery swapping. On October 22, BAIC and CATL signed a comprehensive agreement to deepen cooperation in battery swapping business. Multiple brand-adapted models under BAIC will be connected to CATL's Chocolate Battery Swapping Ecosystem. The two sides will jointly build a nationwide, highly interconnected public energy replenishment infrastructure network in the future. The question that follows is: with the advancement of ultra-fast charging technology and the gradual popularization of ultra-fast charging stations, the charging time of new energy vehicles has been continuously shortened, and the gap in energy replenishment time between charging and battery swapping is also narrowing. Why are so many automakers ramping up their investment in battery swapping? Ultra-fast Charging is Speeding Up, and Battery Swapping is Gaining Momentum Although at the early stage of the birth of new energy vehicles, automakers represented by BAIC and NIO began to deploy battery swapping technology, this solution has never become the mainstream energy replenishment method. The reason is that due to the separation of batteries and vehicles, compared with fast charging technology, the operation chain involved in battery swapping solutions is more complex. On the one hand, automakers cannot "work behind closed doors" and need to carry out overall design for models, batteries and battery swapping stations. As battery technology evolves rapidly, batteries of various models and specifications emerge in an endless stream, and battery swapping solutions will limit the technological iteration of automakers to a certain extent. Source: NIO On the other hand, in the context where cross-brand compatibility and network sharing are not yet sufficient, automakers need to bear large investment in station construction and operation, and large-scale promotion also faces considerable pressure. More importantly, as ultra-fast charging technology matures gradually, the comparative advantage of battery swapping solutions in "fast energy replenishment" will be weakened. Source: BYD For example, in March 2026, BYD launched the second-generation Blade Battery and its flash charging technology, which can achieve 10%-70% charge in 5 minutes, 10%-97% full charge in 9 minutes, and only takes 3 minutes longer than at room temperature at minus 30℃ for 20%-97% charging. The following month, CATL released its third-generation Shenxing ultra-fast charging battery, which delivers equivalent 10C and peak 15C ultra-fast charging capabilities, taking only 6 minutes and 27 seconds to charge from 10% to 98%. Source: Li Auto In April 2023, Ma Donghui, President and Chief Engineer of Li Auto, explained why Li Auto chose ultra-fast charging instead of battery swapping. Because electricity has no physical boundary, but battery swapping requires replacing the entire PACK (battery pack), which has physical boundaries. At the same time, achieving compatibility between different models and different brands is a huge challenge, which does not conform to Li Auto's principle of prioritizing efficiency. Different from the fact that it is difficult to form an effective unified standard for battery swapping, Ma Donghui believes that the charging gun standard is easier to unify and become a public resource, so he "does not think battery swapping can perform better than ultra-fast charging in the promotion of passenger vehicles." All in all, the thresholds such as technical adaptation, station investment and cross-brand collaboration have prevented battery swapping from becoming the mainstream energy replenishment method. The development of ultra-fast charging technology will further weaken the comparative advantage of battery swapping. With brands such as Feifan and Ruilan fading out, only NIO still adheres to the battery swapping technology route in the consumer market before. Lowering Vehicle Purchase Threshold, Battery Rental Solution Has Become a Consensus Since 2026, the battery swapping solution has become increasingly popular, not because the battery swapping technology itself has made considerable progress, but because the market environment of China's new energy vehicles has undergone significant changes. Source: China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) Data disclosed by CPCA shows that in September 2026, the retail sales of passenger vehicles in China reached 1.618 million units, down 28.0% year on year. Among them, the retail sales of new energy vehicles decreased by 16.7% year on year, with a penetration rate of 67%, and the growth of penetration rate began to slow down. Against the background of sluggish retail performance in China's passenger vehicle market, new energy vehicles are also facing the challenge of poor sales. For automakers, in addition to continuing to attract fuel vehicle users, they also need to reduce the initial purchase cost to attract potential consumers who are still on the fence. Source: NIO Since the vehicle and battery can be separated, the battery swapping mode can significantly reduce the price of vehicles. artigo.texto: Can CATL and automakers go back to the way they used to be? On October 21, 2026, CATL's A-share stock price dropped by 12%, marking the second-largest single-day decline since its listing. The Q3 financial report released the previous night showed that the revenue in the third quarter reached 1652 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 58.6%; the net profit attributable to shareholders was 212.5 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 14.5%, while the gross margin declined to some extent. The slowdown in profit growth stems from multiple factors: low-priced long-term energy storage orders signed in the past two years have entered the concentrated delivery period, and the proportion of energy storage sales has risen to about a quarter, leading to double dilution of the overall gross margin from low-margin businesses. In addition, the launch of consumption tax in September and the reduction of export tax rebates also increased the current-period costs. CATL also stated, "We are actively communicating with customers to share the relevant impacts together, and at the same time, we are promoting the implementation of new technologies and new products to reduce the impact on profitability." Negotiating with customers to share costs ostensibly aims to cope with short-term profit pressure, but behind it lies a longer-term issue in the power battery industry chain: how the value of the industry chain is distributed, and who holds the initiative. In the past, CATL occupied a pivotal position in the battery supply chain by virtue of its scale and technological advantages. However, this pattern is not static. In the past month, automakers have taken increasingly intensive actions around self-developed batteries, supplier selection and system integration. The so-called "de-CATL trend" is becoming a new force affecting the division of labor in the industry chain. This does not necessarily put automakers and CATL in opposition, but it may redefine the cooperation boundary between the two sides, and also becomes a key factor affecting CATL's future profit model. Automakers and CATL Start to Redraw Boundaries The "de-CATL trend" consists of a series of specific actions taken by different automakers. Li Auto has gone the farthest in this direction. At the earnings call in March this year, Li Auto stated that starting from 2026, all models of Li Auto will adopt a dual-battery route with both the "Li Auto brand" and the CATL brand. At the interim results call on August 26, Li Xiang said that starting from the second half of this year, Li Auto's self-developed batteries will be successively installed in all models. Later, Li Auto made a strategic capital increase of 2.65 billion yuan in Sunwoda Power. Combined with its previous shareholding, Li Auto holds 11.17% of the shares of Sunwoda Power, making it the second largest shareholder. At a communication meeting in September, representatives of Li Auto reiterated that starting from the new generation L8, all Li Auto models will be equipped with its self-developed batteries. The self-development model of Li Auto brand is that Li Auto takes the lead in cell design and R&D, while battery companies such as Sunwoda and CALB are responsible for cell production and manufacturing. At the battery pack level, BMS, thermal management and even insulating materials are independently developed, designed and produced by Li Auto. Judging from the current list of partners for Li Auto's self-developed batteries, CATL is no longer included. Reflected in the installation data, in June this year, Li Auto was still the fourth largest customer of CATL (accounting for 6.8%) and the fifth largest customer of Sunwoda (accounting for 6.4%). By August, Li Auto disappeared from the top five customers of CATL and became the largest customer of Sunwoda (accounting for 39%). XPeng Motors holds a similar attitude to Li Auto. In September 2026, He Xiaopeng publicly announced that "we will develop batteries independently starting from this year". Its route is similar: it takes the lead in defining the battery system, while cells continue to be purchased from external sources, and suppliers such as CALB and EVE Energy have been introduced. Xiaomi adopts a layered strategy. The newly launched range-extended products Pengcheng N70 and N90 will adopt the "Dragon Armor Battery", while according to previous reports, CATL remains the primary supplier for pure electric models under the main brand such as SU7 and YU7. For the "Dragon Armor Battery", cells are developed and manufactured by CALB and Sunwoda, but the product definition rights of battery pack structure, thermal management and BMS are in the hands of Xiaomi. AITO, which previously had close cooperation with CATL, also broke the pattern of "exclusive supply for all models" in 2026. The announcement from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shows that the pure electric version of AITO M6 has been equipped with an 81kWh LFP battery pack from Gotion High-Tech, and CALB has also entered AITO's supply system. Among traditional automakers, GAC's ENPOWER battery plant has been put into operation, realizing independent R&D and production; Geely integrated its battery assets to establish Jiyao Pass in 2025, and continues to promote independent R&D. Looking back at these actions of automakers, their purpose is not necessarily to kick CATL out of the game. More of them want to reduce their dependence on a single supplier, which does not mean that CATL has lost its product competitiveness. The most important means is to separate "cell procurement" from "battery pack manufacturing". Through this separation, automakers have redrawn the boundary of the supply chain, clarifying which manufacturing links can be outsourced and which definition rights and integration rights must be kept in their own hands, thus changing the power relationship between automakers and battery manufacturers. artigo.texto: The follow-on deal, signed through its U.S. subsidiary Samsung SDI America, lifts the total volume contracted with AOP to 1.5 GWh after an initial order late last year. AOP will deploy the systems, due for delivery by year-end, at a large-scale Texas power project set to break ground next year. The order covers the Samsung Battery Box 1.7, an all-in-one unit built with high-nickel NCA cells at StarPlus Energy, Samsung SDI's Indiana joint venture with Stellantis. It packs 17 percent more energy density than its predecessor into the same 20-foot container and holds NFPA 855 and UL 9540 safety certifications. All three Korean battery makers are retooling U.S. electric vehicle lines for energy storage as EV demand cools, and Samsung SDI's turn has gathered pace this year. It landed a 1.5 trillion won ($1.13 billion) U.S. ESS order in March and agreed in August to buy General Motors' stake in their Indiana joint venture, with storage batteries the near-term priority. Samsung SDI says it is the only non-Chinese maker of prismatic ESS batteries in North America, a format it says outlasts pouch cells in durability and fire safety. The company is in talks with several other U.S. customers and expects further orders soon. "Alpha Omega Power is one of the fastest growing independent power producers in the country, and the kind of sophisticated operator we want to partner with to tackle grid reliability challenges," said Fabrice Hudry, executive vice president and head of the ESS team at Samsung SDI America. He said the company would widen its footing in North America through "differentiated technology and local production capabilities." AJP Takeaways - Samsung SDI said on Oct. 26, 2026 that its U.S. unit had signed a 1 GWh energy storage supply deal with Alpha Omega Power, bringing their total contracts to 1.5 GWh. - The SBB 1.7 units will be made at StarPlus Energy in Indiana, Samsung SDI's joint venture with Stellantis, for a Texas power project due to break ground in 2027. - The order follows Samsung SDI's 1.5 trillion won U.S. ESS deal in March 2026 and its August 2026 agreement to buy General Motors' stake in their Indiana battery joint venture. artigo.texto: Samsung SDI has secured a 1-gigawatt-hour energy storage system supply deal with US power developer Alpha Omega Power, bringing their combined contracts to 1.5 GWh as the Korean battery maker expands its North American business. The latest agreement, signed through Samsung SDI's Michigan-based subsidiary, follows an initial deal made last year, the company said Monday. The StarPlus Energy plant in Kokomo, Indiana, will produce the battery cells and modules, with deliveries scheduled by year-end. Samsung SDI will supply its Samsung Battery Box 1.7, an integrated ESS solution using high-nickel nickel-cobalt-aluminum prismatic batteries. The system offers 17 percent higher energy density than its predecessor, SBB 1.5, within the same 20-foot container. It also features AI-based monitoring to detect abnormalities and predict battery life. For fire protection, SBB 1.7 uses Samsung SDI's Enhanced Direct Injection technology, which delivers fire-extinguishing agents directly into battery modules. The company said the system complies with US fire safety standard NFPA 855 and holds UL 9540 certification. AOP plans to deploy the batteries at large-scale power projects in the western US and Texas, where construction is expected to begin next year. The projects aim to support grid reliability as electricity demand rises. "American-made ESS from Samsung SDI will play an important role in AOP's continued growth," said Alpha Omega Power CEO Paul Choi. "This second agreement strengthens our domestic supply chain supporting the next generation of energy infrastructure." Samsung SDI is seeking additional ESS contracts in North America, positioning its locally manufactured prismatic batteries as an alternative to Chinese suppliers. Fabrice Hudry, head of Samsung SDI America's ESS team, said the company plans to expand its regional business by leveraging its battery technology and US production capabilities. yejinlim@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: Key Takeaways - HiTHIUM, a stationary energy storage manufacturer with more than 200 GWh of cumulative deliveries, has formally entered the Canadian market with Toronto as its main hub. - The company is offering a 4-hour system built on its 6.25 MWh “∞Power” container and a 6.9 MWh 8-hour lithium-ion system that it describes as the first native 8-hour lithium-ion product. - A new 4 MWh sodium-ion system supporting 2 to 8 hours of storage is aimed at very cold regions such as Northern Canada. - HiTHIUM has offices in British Columbia and Alberta, plus sites in Quebec, Yellowknife and Fort Smith. - A UL Solutions fire test at the start of 2026 left the burning 6.25 MWh container structurally intact, with no thermal propagation to units placed 15 cm away. HiTHIUM has announced its entry into Canada, bringing 4-hour and 8-hour battery energy storage systems (BESS) and a sodium-ion product built for extreme cold to a market that is adding grid-scale storage quickly. The Toronto-based launch was announced on Oct. 21, 2026. HiTHIUM Sets Up Canadian Operations The manufacturer works only on stationary energy storage and says it ranks among the top two suppliers worldwide for storage components, with cumulative delivered capacity now above 200 GWh. Toronto will serve as the center of its Canadian business. HiTHIUM also runs subsidiary offices in British Columbia and Alberta, along with operating sites in Quebec and in the northern communities of Yellowknife and Fort Smith. Storage Demand in Canada According to the company, Canada’s installed storage base is expected to double between 2025 and 2027, while combined wind, solar and storage capacity in the country is projected to hit 50 GW by 2035. The company is pitching its utility-scale products into that buildout, which is part of the wider growth covered on the iGrowNews battery storage news page. Alongside its lithium-ion lineup, the company introduced a 4 MWh sodium-ion system. HiTHIUM says the product is built for a very long service life, can be configured for 2 to 8 hours of storage, and suits harsh, cold climates like those in Canada’s north. HiTHIUM Executives on the Canadian Push “We are committed to delivering Canadian customers advanced, robust solutions, from 8-hour long duration energy storage to extreme-weather-ready sodium-ion BESS. But this also means being present for customers wherever they are, able to serve them quickly and locally. While Toronto serves as the main hub for our Canadian operations, we have subsidiary offices in British Columbia and Alberta, as well as operating sites in Quebec, Yellowknife, and Fort Smith,” said Mizhi Zhang, President of Global Business at HiTHIUM. “Canada’s ambitious clean energy targets, as well as its high safety and regulatory standards, require partners who can deliver advanced technology that’s also tested and compliance-ready. At the same time, project developers have to consider the tough climate. As a vertically integrated, global solutions provider, HiTHIUM is structured to meet exactly this nexus of challenges. Our strategy of advancing both lithium-ion and sodium-ion storage is designed to offer customers in markets like Canada the benefits of flexibility, since we see these technologies as highly complementary,” Zhang added. “Our partners, whether major energy developers, public utilities, or industrial enterprises, rely on our readiness for local certification and our long-term bankability to support them, from permitting through project commissioning,” said Jordan Hebbert, Senior Manager of Canada at HiTHIUM. “Likewise, they depend on the proven durability of HiTHIUM technology—including performance even in extreme weather conditions. In fact, long-term operational data from North American and European projects has recently demonstrated systems outperforming even our guarantees. And we offer customers a wider range of durations and choice of chemistries because we understand that they’re coming to us with a very diverse range of energy storage needs,” Hebbert said. Matching Duration to Project Needs The 4-hour offering is based on the “∞Power” 6.25 MWh container, which uses a 1175 Ah cell made by HiTHIUM. The company says most projects now planned in Canada are sized around this 4-hour unit, which lets operators move wind, solar and baseload generation into later peak periods, support grid reliability and absorb more renewable output as electrification pushes demand up. The design packs more capacity into a standard 20-foot container, and units can be installed back-to-back and side-to-side to shrink a site’s footprint. HiTHIUM’s 8-Hour Lithium-Ion System For longer discharge, HiTHIUM offers a 6.9 MWh 8-hour BESS using its own 1300 Ah cells. The company says the system uses fewer parts, carries a 25-year lifespan and is intended to reduce renewable curtailment and serve industries that cannot tolerate downtime, such as AI data centers. HiTHIUM argues that wind developers and data center operators can both gain lower risk and steadier revenue from 8-hour storage, a theme that runs through much of the renewable energy sector. Fire Test Results Early in 2026, HiTHIUM and UL Solutions carried out an independent fire test on the safety design of the 6.25 MWh block. One container burned under extreme conditions for 24 hours with its doors open to maximize heat spread, while neighboring containers sat only 15 cm away and only passive safety systems were active. After the test, the burned container remained structurally intact, fire did not spread between containers, and cell temperatures in the adjacent units stayed below safety limits, according to the company.
