artigo.texto: Superexcesso de data centers de IA até 2028? O que a SemiAnalysis diz sobre a oferta de GPUs e restrições de energia A supercapacidade dos centros de dados de IA pode se tornar uma preocupação significativa até 2028, pois a rápida expansão da infraestrutura gera incerteza em relação à oferta de GPUs, disponibilidade de eletricidade e demanda por computação. Em sua pesquisa de 19 de outubro de 2026, a SemiAnalysis projetou mais de 50 gigawatts (GW) de capacidade adicional de centros de dados globais em 2027, levantando questões sobre se a produção de semicondutores poderá acompanhar a construção. O possível desequilíbrio pode afetar a Nvidia, grandes provedores de nuvem e investidores que financiam o desenvolvimento da infraestrutura de IA. No entanto, as atuais escassezes de eletricidade e a forte demanda por serviços de inteligência artificial complicam as perspectivas. Compreender a relação entre capacidade de centros de dados, disponibilidade de chips avançados e requisitos futuros de computação é essencial para avaliar os riscos financeiros e as oportunidades de crescimento do setor. SemiAnalysis alerta para possível supercapacidade de data centers de IA até 2028 A empresa de pesquisa de semicondutores SemiAnalysis alertou que os centros de dados de IA podem enfrentar supercapacidade até 2028, à medida que a construção de infraestrutura acelera e as restrições de fornecimento de semicondutores evoluem. Em seu relatório de 19 de outubro de 2026, a empresa previu mais de 50 gigawatts (GW) de capacidade adicional de centros de dados globais em 2027. O líder da pesquisa, Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros, destacou posteriormente a possibilidade de que o desenvolvimento de centros de dados possa acabar superando a disponibilidade de hardware de computação avançado. O alerta refere-se a um possível desequilíbrio entre a capacidade da infraestrutura e o fornecimento de chips, e não a uma redução confirmada na demanda por inteligência artificial. SemiAnalysis prevê mais de 50 GW de capacidade de data centers em 2027 Em seu relatório de 19 de outubro, Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, a SemiAnalysis elevou sua previsão de expansão de capacidade para 2027 de aproximadamente 43 GW para mais de 50 GW. A pesquisa identificou mais de 24 GW de capacidade de data centers em construção avançada em 40 grandes complexos, com a maioria dessa capacidade prevista para ser entregue durante 2027. Muitas dessas instalações já estavam mais da metade do caminho na construção, com equipamentos elétricos e de refrigeração instalados. Os achados sustentam as expectativas de expansão substancial da infraestrutura de IA, embora a atividade de construção projetada não garanta que todas as instalações se tornem operacionais conforme o cronograma. A SemiAnalysis baseou suas projeções em monitoramento da construção em nível de edifício, atividade de desenvolvimento de hyperscalers, compromissos de locação e indicadores de implantação de equipamentos. Grandes empresas de tecnologia, incluindo Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta e Oracle, contribuíram para o aumento da demanda por instalações de computação em grande escala. Os desenvolvedores também estão adotando construção modular e sistemas elétricos pré-fabricados para reduzir os prazos dos projetos e diminuir a necessidade de mão de obra. Essas melhorias podem acelerar a adição de capacidade, mas as condições de financiamento, conexões elétricas e disponibilidade de equipamentos permanecem como fatores importantes que influenciam as datas reais de conclusão. O risco de superoferta de data centers de IA depende da oferta de chips e da expansão da infraestrutura Durante uma discussão em 20 de outubro de 2026, o pesquisador da SemiAnalysis Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros destacou a relação em mudança entre a disponibilidade de GPUs e a oferta de energia elétrica para centros de dados. Em alguns mercados, obter GPUs tornou-se mais fácil do que garantir energia suficiente para operá-las, deixando a infraestrutura elétrica como uma grande restrição à implantação. No entanto, à medida que os desenvolvedores expandem instalações e introduzem geração de energia no local, a indústria poderia enfrentar um gargalo diferente. Chips de lógica avançada, memória de alta largura de banda e capacidade de fabricação de semicondutores podem se tornar cada vez mais importantes para determinar quão rapidamente novos centros de dados podem ser equipados com sistemas de IA operacionais. O risco potencial de supercapacidade de data centers de IA em 2028 surgiria se as instalações concluídas excedessem a oferta disponível de equipamentos de computação adequados. Os operadores poderiam, consequentemente, enfrentar infraestrutura elétrica, de refrigeração e de edifícios subutilizadas enquanto aguardam a instalação de GPUs ou componentes de suporte. Tal descompasso poderia atrasar a geração de receita e aumentar a pressão financeira sobre projetos intensivos em capital, mesmo que a demanda por serviços de computação de IA continue crescendo. Se esse cenário se materializar dependerá da produção de semicondutores, da comissionamento das instalações, da disponibilidade de eletricidade e das necessidades de computação dos clientes. O aviso da SemiAnalysis permanece como uma perspectiva condicional, e não como confirmação de que a infraestrutura global de IA entrou em um ciclo de superoferta. Restrições de oferta e energia da GPU criam novos gargalos na infraestrutura de IA A rápida expansão da inteligência artificial está exercendo pressão crescente sobre as redes elétricas, a fabricação de semicondutores e a infraestrutura de computação avançada. Embora as empresas estejam investindo pesadamente em aceleradores de IA e novas instalações, a disponibilidade de GPUs sozinha não determina quanta capacidade de computação pode se tornar operacional. Os data centers exigem eletricidade confiável, refrigeração de alta densidade, equipamentos de rede e memória especializada para suportar cargas de trabalho modern

artigo.texto: *This content was translated by AI.View Original The third-quarter net profit growth rate of Ningde Times (, hereinafter referred to as CATL), China’s largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer, recorded its lowest level in nearly two years due to the slowing pace of Chinese auto sales and intensifying competition in the battery market. According to a public disclosure on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, CATL’s third-quarter net profit rose 14.5% year-on-year to 21.2 billion yuan (approximately $3.17 billion). This figure significantly fell short of the 41.2% growth expected by analysts, as aggregated by LSEG SmartEstimate. The growth rate slowed further following a 36.5% increase in the previous quarter, the second quarter. Third-quarter revenue increased 58.6% year-on-year to 165.2 billion yuan, though it fell short of the market-expected 60.2% growth. However, it marked a slight rise compared to the previous quarter’s revenue growth rate of 56.9%. The primary drivers of the slowdown in profitability arethe decline in domestic market share and intensified competition. According to industry data, CATL’s market share in China’s power battery installation market fell from 49.8% in January to 40.9% in September. Meanwhile, competitor BYD expanded its share over the same period from 17.4% to 21.1%, narrowing the gap. However, overseas market expansion is supporting growth. Based on global electric vehicle battery usage from January to August this year, CATL’s market share reached 39.4%, up from 37.7% in the same period last year. In contrast, BYD, ranked second, saw its global share decline from 17.1% to 15.1%. Meanwhile, CATL recently unveiled next-generation batteries for heavy-duty trucks and announced plans to expand its battery swap network. Industry observers expect CATL’s energy storage segment, which currently accounts for approximately one-quarter of its global revenue, to expand to about half by 2030. *This content was translated by AI.View Original

artigo.texto: PERU — Jason McClure, an apple farmer in Miami County, said he didn’t have any plans to run for political office this year. But that changed when the Miami County Plan Commission voted in May to give a favorable recommendation to a data center ordinance and lift a temporary moratorium on the projects. Hundreds of residents attended the meeting to speak out against it. That included McClure, who wants to reinstate the moratorium. The day after the meeting, he went to the courthouse to file as an independent to challenge two-term Republican County Commissioner Fred Musselman, who serves on the board and voted to pass the ordinance. “It was the straw that broke my back to get into the race,” McClure said. “Enough is enough. My neighbors are showing up and they’re not being heard.” ‘This election’s boogeyman’ As proposals to build hyperscale data centers rapidly ramp up across Indiana, the controversial developments have become the defining issue in many local races where elected officials are considering the issue. Voters are asking whether candidates for county commissioner and council seats support or oppose data centers. For some, the answer will determine their vote, according to Chad Kinsella, director of Ball State University’s Bowen Center for Public Affairs. “Data centers have kind of become this election cycle’s boogeyman,” he said. “It seems to be that everybody hates them and is terrified that one’s going to show up in their vicinity.” At the beginning of the year, Indiana had 38 operational data centers and 37 more under construction or planned for development, according to the University of Virginia’s Weldon Cooper Center for Public Service. A number of large-scale projects have been proposed or approved since then, including in Kokomo, Hobart, Wheatfield, Frankfort and Sullivan County. Nearly 70% of likely voters in Indiana say they oppose construction of new data centers, according to a Free Press Indiana Poll conducted by Bellwether Research. Just 18% said they supported more construction and 13% were unsure. Shannon McFarland, who lives in Peru, which is located in Miami County, said she strongly opposes a data center anywhere in the county. She said that’s the only reason she’s voting for McClure, the independent candidate who wants a moratorium. “Most of this town does not want them here,” McFarland said. “I will absolutely vote for McClure.” In rural Jasper County, commissioners in June unanimously approved a development agreement with Amazon to build a $7 billion, 304-acre data center campus near Wheatfield. Resident Shawna Reid said she strongly opposes the project and wishes she could vote against Rein Bontreger, the incumbent Republican commissioner on the ballot, but he’s running unopposed. With no option to vote for an alternate candidate, Reid is pushing her state legislators to draft a law to allow Hoosiers to vote out commissioners for “serious misconduct” before their term is up. “If you don’t have a say in pulling them out of there if they have committed some travesty while they’re in office, that’s not cool,” Reid said. Guardrails or bans? Voters will decide But some county commissioners running for office are banking on voters who are more open to data center developments showing up at the polls. Angela Henzman, the Democratic candidate for LaPorte County commissioner, said she has concerns about data centers, but thinks an outright ban or moratorium isn’t the answer. The issue is top of mind for residents there. Amazon is building a $1 billion data center campus in the city of La Porte, and Google has plans to build a 70-acre project in Michigan City. Henzman said she’s pushing for any new projects to be built in an industrial park in the county under tight restrictions aimed at protecting residents and the environment. “There’s a small group of people who will say, ‘I’m 100% against that,’” Henzman said. “But then there are so many people along the spectrum that are saying, ‘I understand they’re here. I just don’t want them on farmland, or near my kids’ schools or near my home.’” Jody Slabaugh, the Republican running for the LaPorte County commissioner seat, said he thinks most voters are against any more data centers coming. He’s proposing a moratorium on new developments — something 32 other counties around Indiana have adopted. “There’s definitely some that are going to say, ‘No, I don’t want a data center, and I’m not voting for anybody who says they’re going to put one here,’” Slabaugh said. A poll released this month commissioned by the American Infrastructure Alliance found a majority of Americans prefer stricter data center guardrails over moratoriums. Nearly 55% of voters said they favor allowing data center construction if the company pays for its own electricity needs to protect ratepayers and guarantees it will protect environmental resources. Less than a third (31%) of those polled called for outright bans. Musselman, the Republican incumbent in Miami County facing off against independent McClure, said he doesn’t regret passing the controversial data center ordinance there. He said it creates reasonable guardrails to protect residents while still reaping projects’ economic benefits, like new jobs and increased tax revenue. Musselman said they’ll find out soon whether more residents support his approach over a straightforward moratorium on the developments. “I guess that’s what Nov. 3 is going to tell,” he said. “If I lose, I was wrong in how I read the community. If I win, I must have been right. I don’t know how else to say it.” FPI News reporter Carson Gerber covers pressing issues throughout the state and how local communities are tackling those challenges. artigo.texto: BYD’s Rolls-Royce rival is almost ready to go — and it could be the world's first to use solid-state battery tech New flagship sedan eyes up the world's leading luxury brands - High-end electric sedan aims to rival Rolls-Royce, Mercedes-Benz and BMW - Quad-motor platform and solid-state battery tech rumored - Flagship model is due to be unveiled in Dubai in November Chinese EV maker BYD has been teasing a number of photos in the lead up to the launch of one of its most luxurious and technologically accomplished model to date. It is understood that BYD’s luxury sub-brand, Yangwang, will be the badge on the hood of the upcoming vehicle, codenamed “Project Hu” that, even in its extensive camouflage, can easily be recognized as a Rolls-Royce or BMW i7 rival. Yangwang general manager Hu Xiaoqing revealed photos of the vehicle earlier this month, while China's ThinkerCar X account also posted videos suggesting it's undergoing final testing. The long, luxurious electric sedan is tipped to feature massive coach doors, which are rear-hinged to make it much easier to clamber in and out, while the predicted 5.5m length is large enough to see it go toe-to-toe with the Mercedes-Maybach S-Class and the Huawei/JAC-built Maextro S800, according to CarNewsChina. There is no confirmation on the powertrain that will underpin the model, but speculation suggests it will pack Yangwang’s quad-motor architecture and DiSus active suspension. It is also hotly-tipped to be one of the first production models to be released with the BYD Group’s solid-state battery technology, while teaser images show it next to BYD's Flash Charge technology, suggesting top-ups could take a matter of minutes. During a recent interview, BYD’s executive vice president Stella Li revealed that the company’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries will debut in 2027, which coincides with a suggested launch date for the Project Hu vehicle. Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more. It also makes sense given that prices for the Hu are rumored to start in the two million yuan range, or about $300,000 / £225,000 / AU$430,000, according to Electrek, which would help cover the cost the expensive, non-mass produced solid-state battery tech. Analysis: Even the luxury market isn't safe The fact that BYD is choosing to unveil Project Hu in Dubai next month suggests that it is confident that its products can rival some of the most luxurious and globally-recognized automotive badges on sale in the world today. CarNewsChina states that YangWang already offers a U8 (the marque’s enormous premium SUV) in the Middle East for 659,900 AED — or around $180,000 / £134,860 / AU$256,420 — which greatly undercuts things like the Bentley Bentayga and Rolls-Royce Cullinan. If BYD’s products genuinely stand up to the industry benchmarks, prestige western brands could soon have to fend off the same sort of competition that is causing headaches for manufacturers in the fiercely ruthless mass markets. artigo.texto: Vantage Data Center holding open house in Oregon Sunday OREGON, Ohio (WTVG) - Vantage Data Centers is hosting an open house to answer questions about its proposed $1 billion dollar data center near Corduroy and Wynn roads. The City of Oregon is encouraging residents to go to Clay High School from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. to ask questions and give feedback. The open house will be on the second floor of Clay High School on 5665 Seaman Road. According to Vantage Data Center’s economic development agreement, the company wants Oregon City Council to approve their project by Oct. 26. Oregon residents will also be voting on Nov. 3 that could possibly restrict the size of the data center. “We believe the project aligns with the city’s vision for development within the industrial zone and can deliver meaningful value to the citizens of Oregon,” a Vantage spokesperson previously told 13 Action News. “We respect the community’s role in this process and understand the city intends to wait for the outcome of the November ballot measure before making decisions about the project timeline. artigo.texto: EMA seeks industry proposals to scale up energy storage Submissions are due by 29 January 2027. The Energy Market Authority (EMA) has launched a consultation paper, calling on the industry to propose technologies, business models, and projects for energy storage systems (ESS) that can be commercially deployed at scale. The development comes as Singapore aims to triple its energy storage capacity from about 350 megawatt-hours to around 1 gigawatt-hour by 2030. Electricity demand is expected to grow rapidly over the next few years, driven by new large loads such as semiconductors, data centres, and the electrification of the transport system, according to EMA. The ESS can respond quickly to fluctuations in solar generation and other supply disruptions to help maintain the power system’s stability. Electricity stored in ESS can also be released should there be high demand in some areas, reducing the strain on the electricity network. Smaller ESS in homes, businesses, and electric vehicles could be coordinated to collectively support the country’s power system, including through arrangements known as virtual power plants. “Singapore’s need for flexibility in the power system is growing,” said Puah Kok Keong, chief executive of EMA. “We would like to partner [with] companies to turn promising ideas into commercially viable energy storage solutions that can be deployed at scale,” he added. EMA said it will work with the industry and relevant agencies to improve access to energy market information and review existing rules. It will also develop requirements for how ESS operate and enable them to be centrally controlled when needed, depending on their size and role in the power system. The authority is also seeking industry interest in forming an industry-led energy storage workgroup to share experiences, develop practical solutions, and address common barriers to ESS deployment. The consultation paper is available on the EMA website, and parties are invited to submit their views and proposals by 29 January 2027 to [email protected].

artigo.texto: Assim, o Comitê Popular da Cidade designou o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente para processar os dossiês e aconselhar o Comitê Popular da Cidade a considerar e aprovar os resultados da resolução de 03 procedimentos: Registro de uma conta no Sistema Nacional de Registro de Cotas de Emissão de Gases de Efeito Estufa e Créditos de Carbono (código 1.014129); cancelamento do registro voluntário de crédito de carbono (código 2.002848); transferência de propriedade de cotas de emissão de gases de efeito estufa e créditos de carbono fora do sistema de comércio de carbono (código 2.002849). Atribuição de responsabilidades para o recebimento e processamento de procedimentos administrativos relacionados a créditos de carbono especializados nas áreas de Indústria e Comércio, Construção, Agricultura e Meio Ambiente. (Hochiminhcity.gov.vn) – O Comitê Popular da Cidade de Ho Chi Minh emitiu um documento atribuindo a responsabilidade pelo recebimento e processamento dos procedimentos administrativos relacionados a créditos de carbono especializados nos setores de Indústria e Comércio, Construção, Agricultura e Meio Ambiente. Para os quatro procedimentos, o registro/ajuste de projetos no âmbito do mecanismo nacional de troca de créditos de carbono (código 1.014136); alterações nos participantes do projeto (código 1.014131); cancelamento do registro do projeto (código 1.014132) e emissão de créditos de carbono no âmbito do mecanismo nacional de troca de créditos de carbono (código 1.014133) são realizados da seguinte forma: Para créditos de carbono especializados sob a responsabilidade de gestão estatal de um departamento que administra um setor ou área específica: o Departamento de Indústria e Comércio, o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente e o Departamento de Construção são designados para processar os dossiês e assessorar o Comitê Popular da Cidade para revisar e aprovar os resultados da resolução desses procedimentos, de acordo com suas respectivas áreas de gestão. Para créditos de carbono multissetoriais sob a responsabilidade de gestão de dois ou mais departamentos/setores: o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente assumirá a liderança, coordenando-se com o Departamento de Indústria e Comércio e o Departamento de Construção para processar os dossiês e assessorar o Comitê Popular da Cidade na aprovação dos resultados para os setores relevantes; o Departamento de Indústria e Comércio assumirá a liderança, coordenando-se com o Departamento de Construção para processar os dossiês dos setores sob sua gestão; os departamentos relevantes precisam coordenar-se e fornecer feedback por escrito em tempo hábil para garantir o andamento do processamento dos dossiês e são responsáveis por questões técnicas. O Comitê Popular da Cidade atribui ao Centro de Serviços Administrativos Públicos da Cidade, subordinado ao Gabinete do Comitê Popular da Cidade, a responsabilidade de receber, processar e devolver os resultados dos procedimentos administrativos. Caso surjam dificuldades que ultrapassem sua competência, as unidades devem encaminhar as informações ao Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente para obter auxílio. Veja os detalhes aqui. artigo.texto: DETROIT, Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Battery Show and Electric & Hybrid Vehicle Technology Expo North America announced the winners for The Battery Awards 2026 honoring standout innovations, technologies, and leaders driving progress across the battery, EV, and energy storage industry. The awards ceremony brought together top manufacturers, engineers, and innovators to celebrate breakthroughs shaping the future of energy storage and electrification. "The Battery Show Awards do more than spotlight the newest innovations, and products in the industry. They connect the people shaping this sector with the insight they need to understand where it's headed," says John Lewinski, Executive Vice President, Manufacturing, Informa. "Our nominees and winners continue to push battery technology, EV infrastructure, ESS to new heights, setting the pace for an industry that's moving faster than ever." Battery Innovation of the Year : Recognizing groundbreaking advancement in battery technology (e.g., solid-state, lithium-metal, novel chemistry). Winner: Sodium Anode Free Battery, Mana Battery Sustainability & Circular Economy Excellence Award : Recognizing leadership in eco-conscious production, recycling, or design. Winner: Honda Mobile Power Pack e (MPP), Honda Battery Manufacturer of the Year : Recognizing outstanding performance in production scale, quality, and innovation. Winner: Torus GigaOne, Torus Aerospace Battery System of the Year Recognizing innovative battery systems that meet the demanding energy density, weight, performance, and safety requirements of aerospace applications. Winner: 800V Battery Cell Simulation Tower, Bloomy Controls, Inc. Battery Safety Technology of the Year : Recognizing innovations that prevent or mitigate thermal runaway and safety risks. Winner: CoolTherm® SF-1000 Syntactic Foam, Parker Lord Battery Startup of the Year : Recognizing an emerging battery company demonstrating exceptional innovation, commercial potential, and the ability to address critical industry challenges through new technologies, products, or business models. Winner: Firoozeh Flow – Intuitive Operator Training and Qualification for Battery Cell Manufacturing, Firoozeh Flow EV Design Excellence Award : Recognizing outstanding achievements in EV design that successfully blend aesthetics, functionality, and user experience. Winner: GEN4 Formula E Car, Paysafe Envision Formula E Team EV Charging Innovation Excellence Award : Recognizing groundbreaking advancements in EV charging technology that significantly improve charging speed, reliability, accessibility, or user experience. Winner: Battery Configuration Switch (BCS), Eaton Grid-Scale Energy Storage Project of the Year : Recognizing an outstanding grid-scale energy storage project that advances grid reliability, resilience, flexibility, or renewable energy integration. Winner: Gotion Gigafactory, Gotion Illinois Battery Manufacturing Technology Award : Recognizing an innovative manufacturing technology, process, or equipment solution that improves battery production efficiency, quality, safety, scalability, or cost. Winner: FormationIQ incorporating Syntropic Cell Technology®, syntrotec GmbH Battery Materials Innovation of the Year : Recognizing a breakthrough in battery materials that improve performance, safety, sustainability, cost, or manufacturability. Winner: IonPrime™ Electrolytes, Elementium Materials Battery Software & Digital Innovation of the Year : Recognizing innovative software, AI, data analytics, simulation, or digital solutions that advance battery development, manufacturing, performance, or lifecycle management. Winner: AQVolt26, SandboxAQ Battery Supply Chain Excellence Award : Recognizing outstanding leadership in strengthening the battery supply chain through sourcing, localization, traceability, logistics, resilience, or strategic partnerships. Winner: Amprius Battery Supply Chain, Amprius Technologies Battery Pack Innovation of the Year : Recognizing an innovative battery pack design or technology that advances performance, safety, energy density, thermal management, integration, or manufacturability. Winner: Project Mammoth: "X-Pack," Echion Technologies Ltd Battery Management System (BMS) Innovation of the Year : Recognizing an innovative battery management system that improves battery safety, performance, reliability, efficiency, diagnostics, or lifetime. Winner: Fusion Series, Associated Environmental Systems Robert Galyen — a visionary leader, distinguished engineer, and globally recognized thought leader in battery energy storage—was honored with a Lifetime Achievement Award. Going forward, this award will honor an individual whose decades-long career has left a lasting mark on the industry through technical excellence, manufacturing leadership, standards development, mentorship, and global vision. About The Battery Show by Informa: The Battery Show is the largest and most comprehensive advanced battery technology event, co-located with Electric & Hybrid Vehicle Technology Expo, the only trade show and conference exclusively dedicated to advanced battery and the electric and hybrid vehicle drivetrain. Visitors to our shows can discover and demo the latest products, technology, and solutions from nearly a thousand suppliers, network with tens of thousands of attendees and access a breadth of education across multiple tracks and technical sessions. The Battery Show is organized by Manufacturing by Informa and includes The Battery Show Europe, The Battery Show North America, The Battery Show India, The Battery Show Asia, and The Battery Show Middle East. Listed media partners include Informa Market's Battery Technology and DesignNews. For more information, please visit manufacturing.informamarkets.com/. artigo.texto: The battery storage system has a power output of 3.7 megawatts, which it can sustain for just over an hour. The photovoltaic system, commissioned in December 2025, comprises 11,132 solar modules and has a capacity of more than 5 megawatts (MWp). Connecting the battery to the new PV system allows the electricity generated to be used even when the sun is not shining. The new photovoltaic system can cover up to 45 percent of BVB's electricity needs at SIGNAL IDUNA PARK. Carsten Cramer, Chairman of the Management Board of Borussia Dortmund: "SIGNAL IDUNA PARK is not only our iconic home, but also a central element of our comprehensive decarbonisation strategy. Together with RWE, we are completing a forward-looking energy concept with this battery storage system, enabling us to make even better use of our solar power. We are delighted that our stadium will continue to stand for greater resource efficiency and innovation." Dr Markus Krebber, CEO of RWE AG: "With the commissioning of the battery storage system, the combined photovoltaic and battery system at SIGNAL IDUNA PARK is now fully operational. Connecting the two systems allows the solar power generated on site to be used even more flexibly—even when the sun is not shining. Through this project, the experts at BVB and RWE have brought our partnership to life and filled it with energy. A strong foundation for further joint developments." artigo.texto: CCUS: Eliminando gargalos para alcançar a meta de emissões líquidas zero. A tecnologia de captura, utilização e armazenamento de CO₂ (CCUS) abre caminhos para a redução de emissões nas indústrias, mas exige a superação de obstáculos relacionados a marcos legais, capital e infraestrutura. Na manhã de 27 de outubro, sob a direção do Ministério da Agricultura e Meio Ambiente , o jornal Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, em colaboração com o Departamento de Mudanças Climáticas e o Instituto de Petróleo do Vietnã (VPI), organizou o workshop “Tecnologia de Captura, Utilização e Armazenamento de CO₂ (CCUS): Uma Solução para Promover o Net Zero no Vietnã”. Estrutura legal completa, avalie com precisão o potencial O Sr. Luong Quang Huy, Chefe do Departamento de Gestão de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa e Proteção da Camada de Ozono (Agência de Alterações Climáticas), afirmou que o período de 2026 a 2030 foi identificado como um período de redução acelerada das emissões, enquanto se aperfeiçoa simultaneamente o quadro operacional do mercado de carbono. De acordo com o roteiro, o Vietname pretende operar oficialmente uma bolsa de créditos de carbono a partir de 2028, criando uma ferramenta adicional para apoiar a concretização das metas climáticas. Neste contexto, a Captura, Utilização e Armazenamento de Carbono (CCUS) é significativa para as indústrias que têm dificuldade em reduzir as emissões através de soluções convencionais. Esta tecnologia permite a captura de CO₂ das fontes de emissão, que pode então ser utilizado ou transportado para um local adequado para armazenamento. Segundo o Global CCS Institute, em 31 de julho de 2026, haverá 113 projetos comerciais de captura e armazenamento de carbono (CCS) em operação no mundo , 59 em construção, 308 em fase avançada de desenvolvimento e 352 em fase inicial de desenvolvimento. A capacidade de captura de CO₂ dos projetos em operação é de aproximadamente 68 milhões de toneladas por ano, enquanto os projetos em construção têm uma capacidade total de cerca de 56 milhões de toneladas por ano. No entanto, a implantação comercial do CCS depende não apenas da disponibilidade da tecnologia, mas também de um arcabouço regulatório e de licenciamento claro, do acesso a locais de armazenamento, da garantia de fluxos de receita e de mecanismos adequados de alocação de riscos ao longo de toda a cadeia de valor. Para o Vietnã, a necessidade de reduzir as emissões nos setores de energia, cimento, aço, química e petróleo e gás exige pesquisa em soluções adaptadas às características específicas de cada setor. O Vietnã possui fontes concentradas de emissão de CO₂, potencial de armazenamento em diversas bacias sedimentares e campos de petróleo e gás offshore em declínio, além da experiência, dados geológicos e capacidades técnicas da indústria de petróleo e gás. Esses são fundamentos cruciais para avaliar a viabilidade do desenvolvimento de CCUS (Captura, Utilização e Armazenamento de Carbono). O Dr. Nguyen Huu Luong, especialista sênior do Instituto de Petróleo do Vietnã, afirmou que o Vietnã possui potencial para armazenar CO₂ em três bacias sedimentares principais: Cuu Long, Nam Con Son e Song Hong. Segundo ele, a Petrovietnam realizou uma avaliação preliminar do potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ em 34 campos de petróleo e gás offshore. Em 2011, o Vietnã realizou a injeção de CO₂ no campo de Rang Dong. No entanto, o potencial geológico não se traduz automaticamente na viabilidade da implementação de um projeto comercial. Cada local precisa ser inspecionado, avaliado e verificado quanto à capacidade de armazenamento, capacidade de absorção de CO₂, integridade do reservatório e condições de monitoramento de segurança a longo prazo. Você também pode gostar Um passo institucional importante é a Lei do Petróleo nº 10/2026/QH16, aprovada pela Assembleia Nacional em 23 de agosto de 2026 e em vigor desde 1º de março de 2027, que adiciona disposições sobre captura e armazenamento de carbono associados às atividades de petróleo e gás. No entanto, para a implementação prática, é necessário esclarecer melhor as normas relativas a levantamentos, seleção de locais, licenciamento de injeção, operação, monitoramento, encerramento de projetos e responsabilidades a longo prazo. O Dr. Nguyen Thanh Tung, Vice-Diretor do Instituto de Petróleo do Vietnã, acredita que as novas regulamentações fornecem uma base legal inicial para que o Vietnã faça a transição da pesquisa potencial para a implementação gradual de projetos. No entanto, essa é apenas uma condição necessária. O arcabouço legal deve abranger todo o ciclo de vida do projeto e esclarecer as responsabilidades de todas as partes envolvidas em cada etapa. A equação entre custo e infraestrutura determina o potencial de comercialização. Além do arcabouço legal, a eficiência econômica é uma das condições decisivas para o desenvolvimento da CCUS (Captura, Utilização e Armazenamento de Carbono). Os custos de captura, transporte, uso e armazenamento de CO₂ precisam ser equilibrados com a receita proveniente de produtos que utilizam CO₂ e com o valor econômico da redução de emissões, incluindo a possibilidade de registro de créditos de carbono, caso as condições aplicáveis sejam atendidas. Segundo o Dr. Nguyen Thanh Tung, um projeto só pode ser implementado em escala comercial quando possui um modelo de negócios viável e um fluxo de receita suficientemente estável para compensar o investimento, os custos operacionais e os riscos. Isso requer um mecanismo para determinar taxas de serviço adequadas, compromissos de longo prazo das fontes de emissão e um plano claro de alocação de riscos entre as partes envolvidas. O Sr. Le Van Nghi, Presidente e CEO da QIS Global, observou que o Vietnã possui vantagens decorrentes de seu potencial de armazenamento de CO₂ offshore, experiência na indústria de petróleo e gás, capacidade em projetar, adquirir, fabricar, comissionar e operar projetos industriais, além de uma rede internacional de cooperação tecnol

artigo.texto: The Pittsburg City Council voted unanimously to place a 45-day moratorium on new data center development following a heated meeting, though residents say the temporary pause does not go far enough to stop a controversial project. The vote targets the next two phases of the Avaio data center project, proposed at the former Delta View Golf Course. The city approved the project's first phase in 2024, which is not affected by the temporary halt. Watch NBC Bay Area News free wherever you are About two dozen demonstrators turned out outside City Hall to protest the development, raising concerns over potential health risks and the project's proximity to homes, schools, and a church. “It’s right by a church, it’s right by a school, I live in close proximity, I’m worried about the illnesses,” said Pittsburg resident Marta Rodrigues. The tension carried inside when demonstrators interrupted the start of the council meeting, prompting a temporary pause. Police escorted the protesters out of the chambers, and the meeting resumed with public comment. Residents continued to press the council during the public comment period, with one commenter stating, "What part of no don’t you understand. I can spell it out for you it’s N-O." Another speaker added, "We can build a future without an industrial power plant besides the playground, protect the places where our children grown up." Councilmembers acknowledged the community's apprehension following the pushback. Local “We hear that there’s a lot of concern….a lot of fear of what it could mean…for city of Pittsburg,” said Councilmember Jelani Killings. The local pushback arrives just days before next week’s election, with Proposition 45 adding another layer of controversy to the debate. Opponents fear the ballot measure could streamline environmental reviews and make it easier to move certain data center projects forward. “It guts our environmental and public review…very broad definition of broadband internet projects,” said Woody Little of Clean and Healthy California. However, a legal analysis from the California Chamber of Commerce challenges that argument, stating that conventional data centers would not qualify under the measure because they do not provide mass-market retail internet access directly to customers. Next Steps The 45-day moratorium takes effect immediately. While the council could consider extending the pause before it expires, development on the first phase of the Avaio project remains unaffected for now.

artigo.texto: A Rivian owner facing repeated outages in Santa Barbara, California, is considering using the truck as a backup power source instead of paying for a conventional home battery install. After getting storage quotes above $20,000, they asked other electric vehicle owners whether a Rivian could handle a small set of essentials when the power cuts out. Here's what to know On Reddit, the owner wrote that their "power goes out several times a year" and said solar battery quotes "keep coming in over $20k." Because the need was limited to one built-in fridge, some lights, and a few small appliances, a cheaper backup option for essentials rather than a whole-home system was seen as the best option. Commenters outlined a range of ways to do that, from simple extension-cord use to generator interlocks, manual transfer switches, and portable batteries that sit between the truck and the home's circuits. One commenter said, "The Rivian inverter has a max of 1500 W," adding that they had relied on extension cords for a freezer and refrigerator during outages. For households dealing with repeated blackouts, adding battery storage is one of the most effective ways to protect a home during outages, lower energy costs, and gain more energy independence. Homeowners comparing options can explore EnergySage for home battery storage choices and competitive installation estimates, and EnergySage has teamed up with electrification brand Qmerit to help homeowners get the best price on home battery storage solutions. More background Cost was a major theme in the thread, especially the difference between installed whole-home battery systems and pieced-together alternatives. The original poster said they had started "to give up" on waiting for bidirectional charging and had seen estimates suggesting a future charger setup could cost about $8,000, which still felt expensive compared with a large portable power bank. A number of replies focused on using a power station as the go-between for the truck and the house. In that setup, the Rivian charges the portable battery, which then feeds a home through a transfer switch or inlet. One commenter said a setup like that can work if household use stays under roughly 1,200 watts while the Rivian charges the buffer battery at about 1,400 watts. The same commenter said they use load shedding for server and network equipment, which "saves me 7kwh a day if i do that." What can be done? Even without official vehicle-to-home capability, some Rivian owners said they have already assembled outage backups around their trucks. That kind of workaround can provide basic backup without the cost of a five-figure installation. It can keep food cold, lights on, and critical devices running while reducing dependence on the grid. The original poster indicated in the thread that they were going to go with the Pecron F5000 system after getting a recommendation from a thread visitor. For readers who want something smaller and less expensive than a whole-home system, Pila is another company offering strong battery backup options. Pila's plug-and-play batteries are priced at a fraction of what a whole-home backup system would cost, which aligns with the thread's focus on lower-cost resilience. Where can I learn more? How to keep essentials powered during an outage is a common topic of discussion. • During an outage, EVs kept the grid operating and proved emergency backup can scale. • GM's push to power homes in blackouts has run into steep install-cost concerns. • More homeowners are installing backup batteries without paying upfront costs through financing. artigo.texto: Did Ukraine's data center strikes affect Russia's bot army? We now have better evidence. Pro-Russian accounts targeting Ukrainians on Facebook and Telegram sharply declined after Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers, according to a new report from a Ukrainian government agency. It’s the most direct evidence so far behind a claim that went viral last week, but it falls well short of proving it. The report comes from Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD), which operates under the country’s National Security and Defense Council. It was published Oct. 15, and United24 Media covered it on Oct. 17. The CCD used software from the Ukrainian security firm Osavul to track accounts it flagged as showing "signs of inauthentic behavior." According to Osavul's website, the firm "builds AI-powered risk intelligence for hybrid threats." According to United24, the CCD analyzed 22,664 messages from 5,201 accounts posted between Oct. 6 and 12, across 26 topics in Ukraine’s information space. The report found two sharp drops in activity, each following a strike that fully shut down a Yandex facility. On Oct. 8, the day a fire took Yandex’s data center in Sasovo, in Russia’s Ryazan region, offline, messages fell 83.6 percent, from 4,032 to 660. You May Also Like The number of active accounts fell by a similar share. Activity rebounded past pre-strike levels by Oct. 10, but on Oct. 12, a day after a strike fully halted operations at a Yandex data center in Vladimir, messages fell by 42.6 percent and active accounts dropped by 41 percent. A smaller group of 98 accounts that posted pro-war propaganda, conspiracy theories, or calls for violence followed the same pattern. The CCD concluded that strikes on data centers can significantly disrupt Russian influence networks, but the effect appears to be short-lived. Mashable was unable to verify the CCD’s findings independently. Before publication, we emailed Osavul to request the underlying dataset, the criteria it uses to flag inauthentic behavior, and any information about where the accounts were hosted. Osavul did not respond by publication time. The report never defines "inauthentic behavior." While the term is quite broad, some general signals that researchers typically attribute to bot accounts include newly created profiles, unusually high posting volume, blank or AI-generated profile photos, and activity across many unrelated political narratives. Without Osavul’s criteria, it’s unclear whether these accounts are automated, run by coordinated humans, or a mix of both. Still, if the numbers hold up, they point to something real. The CCD argues that the drops show strikes on data centers can significantly constrain Russia’s information operations by disrupting the automated networks behind them. However, the agency also acknowledges how quickly the accounts came back, suggesting the disruptions were "substantial but short-lived." Why it matters The findings arrive after a week of overheated claims. Last week, Mashable looked at viral claims that Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers had knocked Russia’s bot army offline. The conclusion we and other outlets reached was that the data behind those claims couldn’t support them. That claim spread like wildfire on social media, amplified by European officials and even backed up by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, President Zelenskyy said "everyone noticed" a drop in Russian bot activity. Social media users echoed similar observations about the seemingly stark decline in pro-GOP and pro-AfD posts after the strikes. It was an easy idea to believe, given how platforms like Facebook and X incentivize and reward polarizing political ragebait, and Russia’s online influence operations are well-documented. The claim also seemed to have supporting data. United24 Media, the Ukrainian government-run outlet whose reporting drove much of the conversation, cited an analysis by The Deep Dive of Cloudflare Radar data. That data showed automated traffic from Yandex’s network had nearly vanished by Oct. 11. As Mashable reported at the time, that data couldn’t support the claim. "Automated traffic" means any request that software, rather than a person, sends to a website, and most of it is mundane. Yandex, often called "Russia's Google," runs the Federation's biggest search engine, so its network constantly sends out crawlers to index the web. Knocking its data centers offline would stop that traffic, whether or not a single troll account went quiet. We found no published evidence tying influence campaigns on social media to Yandex servers, and United24 acknowledged the same limitation. Cloudflare has since published its own analysis. It said its data doesn’t appear to support claims that the strikes crippled social media manipulation, though it couldn’t rule out a connection. Zelenskyy’s office has also narrowed his remarks. According to BBC Verify, his office said the president was "talking about the atmosphere on social media" rather than a fall in bot activity. Topics Cybersecurity Chance Townsend is the General Assignments Editor at Mashable, covering tech, video games, dating apps, digital culture, and whatever else comes his way. He has a Master's in Journalism from the University of North Texas and is a proud orange cat father. His writing has also appeared in PC Mag and Mother Jones. artigo.texto: Insight and analysis on the data center space from industry thought leaders. Rethinking the Blind-Mate Connection PBMC technology helps liquid-cooled servers deliver higher flow in less space while better accommodating alignment variation during installation and service. Much of the conversation around liquid cooling focuses on the system itself. However, higher cooling demands are also changing expectations for the individual components within it. One such component is the connection point between IT equipment and the cooling infrastructure. For server and rack designers, that connection now must do more than simply link two sides of a liquid loop. It must support greater coolant flow, fit within increasingly constrained server-tray space, and accommodate alignment variations that come with real-world installation and removal. Those requirements have helped drive the development of a newer approach to the traditional blind-mate connection: the pivoting blind-mate coupling (PBMC). PBMC technology was developed through collaboration within the Open Compute Project ecosystem and reflects a broader industry effort to address the changing needs of high-performance liquid-cooled systems. Parker Hannifin’s BQC Series is one example of this newer coupling architecture. Why the Connection Needed to Change The development of the PBMC started with a practical set of system-level requirements. Newer rack and server architectures called for greater flow through the connection while reducing the space the coupling occupied in the server tray. The connection also needed more self-alignment capability between the two sides as equipment was inserted and removed. Solving one of those problems can make another more difficult. Increasing flow can push designers toward larger flow paths. Server designers, meanwhile, are trying to preserve as much usable tray space as possible. And because a blind-mate connection is made during installation rather than being manually aligned by a technician, the coupling must also account for the possibility that the plug and socket may not align perfectly every time. PBMC technology was developed to address those requirements as part of the same connection design. Accounting for Real-World Misalignment Blind-mate couplings already solve an important problem in liquid-cooled server systems: they allow a connection to be made as equipment is installed from the front (cold-aisle) side of the system. That matters for more than convenience. The rear (hot-aisle) side of a server rack can contain manifolds, connections, and other equipment operating in a high-temperature environment. Installation and removal from the cold aisle can reduce the need for personnel to reach into the hot aisle to handle connections at the rear of the rack. The tradeoff is that a blind-mate connection does not have a technician guiding the two coupling halves together. Server trays, racks, and manifolds are also not always positioned with perfect precision. Small differences in component location can add up by the time the two sides of the connection meet. A pivoting blind-mate design provides more self-alignment capability as the two sides of the connection come together. Rather than depending as heavily on near-perfect alignment between the two halves, the connection can accommodate a greater degree of positional variation during mating. For system designers, that can reduce the sensitivity of the connection to the normal dimensional variation present throughout the surrounding equipment. That does not mean PBMCs replace every traditional blind-mate connection. They are particularly relevant in server-tray and blade-system applications where self-alignment capability, higher flow, and limited available space all have to be considered together. More Flow Without Giving Up Server-Tray Space Flow performance was another major factor behind the PBMC’s development. As cooling requirements increase, the connection cannot become an unnecessary restriction within the loop. It needs to support the required coolant flow while keeping pressure losses through the connection under control. Simply making every component larger, however, is not an ideal answer. Space inside the server tray is limited, and cooling hardware competes for room with the computing equipment it is meant to support. The length and overall footprint of the coupling therefore become part of the system-design conversation. PBMC designs address that challenge by combining a larger flow path with a compact overall package. The objective is straightforward: support higher flow without requiring designers to give more of the tray to the connection itself. Designing for High-Flow Conditions Higher flow also creates challenges less visible than the connection size. One is seal retention. O-rings and other seals must remain securely positioned as fluid travels through the connection. Under demanding flow and pressure conditions, a poorly retained seal can be pulled from its groove and carried downstream with the system fluid. This condition, often referred to as seal washout, can compromise the connection and create problems elsewhere in the cooling loop. For that reason, seal retention becomes an important design consideration as coupling flow requirements increase. Retention features can help keep seals properly positioned under demanding operating conditions rather than treating them as an afterthought to flow performance. Part of a Broader Shift in Liquid-Cooling Design The value of PBMC technology is not tied to any one feature. Its development reflects how closely connected the requirements within modern liquid-cooling systems have become. Flow affects component size. Component size affects available tray space. Blind mating affects alignment requirements. Higher flow introduces its own mechanical considerations. artigo.texto: MOUNTAIN HOME, Idaho — Mountain Home neighbors are raising concerns about a proposed data center, but the project faces a major obstacle: the city's current zoning regulations don't allow it. WATCH: Where the proposed Mountain Home data center project stands The proposal from Weitz & Co. outlines plans for four three-story data center buildings at the Bennett Ranch Industrial Campus, totaling approximately 3.4 million square feet. The development would also include power generation, backup power systems and cooling infrastructure. Despite the scale of the plans, the project remains just a proposal, with no formal application submitted to the city. In a letter addressed to company owner Dan Weitz, Mayor Rich Sykes said, "On October 20, 2026, [Weitz] dropped off at Mountain Home city hall three copies of what appears to be a proposal," but has not submitted a land-use application, conditional use permit or building permit. "It makes me feel a whole lot better knowing that it's just an idea right now and not something that has been approved and stamped and is going through," Mountain Home neighbor Christine May said. RELATED | Thousands of acres of public land south of Boise eyed for new data center Still, the size of the proposal and its potential impact have some neighbors worried. The developer said, in their project overview documents, its closed-loop cooling system would be designed for minimal water consumption, and an agreement dating back to 2005 would allow the site to connect to the city's water system. But the proposal doesn't spell out what that agreement allows. "All the money in the world will not buy you a glass of water if there isn't any, and we have to think about that," Mountain Home neighbor Lizabeth Braun said. Some neighbors question whether a project this size belongs here at all. "I just don't think they need to be here in Mountain Home. They can try elsewhere," Mountain Home neighbor Evan Peterson said. "I just think that there's a lot of reasons why we shouldn't have a data center in the middle of town surrounded by houses," May said. Months before this proposal showed up at City Hall, Councilman Scott Harjo went to the Planning and Zoning Commission, raising concerns about data centers, including their potential water use. "I'd like to have an answer for that before they come knocking, quite frankly," Harjo said. Now, someone has come knocking. The mayor's letter said the city has been working since early July to define and categorize data centers in its zoning code. Right now, the city said, "Data center is neither a permitted nor conditional use in any zone in the City," meaning they're currently prohibited under city code. READ MORE | Inside Meta’s new Kuna data center built for AI But some neighbors aren't convinced it'll stay that way. "Just judging by their previous reactions to things, I think it probably stands a pretty good chance of getting approved," Braun said. "It's scary when you think about it." "I don't want to see them get walked over. I don't want to see us as a community get walked over," Peterson said. The city said no formal application has been submitted, but the developer can still work with staff and pursue approval once the proper zoning rules are in place. artigo.texto: Sungrow has announced plans to partner with ENGIE and Elecnor to advance the 150MW/300MWh Hazelwood battery energy storage system (BESS) located in Victoria, Australia. Sungrow Australia, a Sungrow subsidiary, will provide the technology, while Elecnor will act as the balance-of-plant (BOP) contractor. Discover B2B Marketing That Performs Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms. The BESS is set to enter commercial operations in 2028. The project plans to use 66 units of Sungrow’s ST5015-UX BESS from its PowerTitan 2.0 series. It will also use 33 SC6900UD-MV power conversion system (PCS) inverters and the company’s EMS3000 smart controller. The new system is designed for utility-scale deployment and will offer high energy density, liquid-cooled thermal management, advanced battery monitoring, and power conversion features to support long-term reliability and safety. Hazelwood BESS 2 will use grid-forming technology designed to help maintain voltage and frequency stability and respond quickly to changes in network conditions. The project partners also expect these capabilities to support the integration of variable renewable generation as its share of electricity supply increases. The system aims to provide flexible energy resources for Victoria and the National Electricity Market (NEM) by storing electricity during periods of low demand and delivering it when needed. Hazelwood BESS 2 represents further development in large-scale battery storage initiatives in Australia, highlighting the involvement of international suppliers such as Sungrow in the country’s move towards an evolving energy system. Sungrow Australia managing director Thomas Hou said: “The Hazelwood BESS 2 represents an important step in advancing grid-forming energy storage in Australia. “Through our collaboration with ENGIE, we aim to bring advanced energy storage technology to support grid stability and enable greater integration of renewable energy. “We look forward to contributing our expertise and supporting the continued development of a more resilient energy system in Victoria.” In August 2026, Sungrow was chosen by Verano Energy to supply a 152MW/606MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) for the Observatorio project in Chile.

artigo.texto: Beijing, 26 out (Xinhua) -- A integração da China entre tecnologias digitais e finanças verdes está abrindo novas oportunidades para a cooperação global na transição de baixo carbono, disseram os participantes na Conferência Anual 2026 do Fórum da Rua Financeira, em Beijing. Sob o tema "Construindo um ecossistema aberto, colaborativo e inclusivo para o desenvolvimento financeiro global", o evento de quatro dias foi encerrado na semana passada. Ele reuniu participantes nacionais e internacionais, tanto online quanto presencialmente, para discutir o desenvolvimento financeiro e a cooperação diante dos desafios econômicos globais. "Nos últimos anos, vimos o mercado de finanças verdes da China crescer várias vezes", disse Ma Jun, presidente do Instituto de Finanças e Sustentabilidade em Beijing. "A integração das finanças digitais e verdes criou muitas oportunidades de crescimento e ajudou a impulsionar os investimentos transfronteiriços." Esse crescimento ganhou reconhecimento internacional. " A China melhorou a qualidade do ar ao desenvolver uma economia circular e construir uma sociedade ambientalmente amigável", disse Yaseen Anwar, ex-presidente do Banco Estatal do Paquistão, em um fórum paralelo. Ele acrescentou que a capacidade instalada de energia eólica e solar do país continua a crescer, enquanto produtos verdes, como veículos de nova energia (NEVs), lideram globalmente. Dados divulgados pelo Ministério da Ecologia e do Meio Ambiente mostram que a capacidade instalada de geração de energia renovável do país atingiu 2,455 bilhões de quilowatts no primeiro semestre deste ano, representando 60,7% de sua capacidade total instalada de geração de energia. A China ocupa o primeiro lugar mundial tanto na produção quanto nas vendas de NEVs há 11 anos consecutivos. Nos últimos anos, a China tem oferecido amplas oportunidades para o investimento verde global e a transição de baixo carbono, aplicando tecnologias como big data, blockchain e IA para melhorar a governança das finanças verdes, modernizar as estruturas industriais e aprimorar o meio ambiente ecológico. O Banco da China emitiu títulos verdes no âmbito da Iniciativa Cinturão e Rota para apoiar grandes projetos verdes, como usinas fotovoltaicas de grande escala em países parceiros. Espera-se que esses projetos forneçam às comunidades locais um abastecimento estável e de longo prazo de energia renovável limpa. O mercado de carbono é uma importante ferramenta política para lidar com as mudanças climáticas por meio de mecanismos de mercado e para acelerar a transformação verde abrangente do desenvolvimento econômico e social. O volume acumulado de negociação de cotas de emissão de carbono no mercado nacional de carbono da China ultrapassou 1 bilhão de toneladas, de acordo com dados do Ministério da Ecologia e do Meio Ambiente. A experiência da China no desenvolvimento de seu mercado de carbono também oferece lições com as quais outros países podem aprender. "Os compromissos da China em relação às emissões de carbono e o desenvolvimento de seu mercado de carbono têm dado uma contribuição enorme para a ação climática global", disse Charles Bowman, copresidente da Força-Tarefa de Finanças Verdes Reino Unido-China. "A cooperação em finanças verdes entre a China e o Reino Unido tem promovido a transformação econômica, a conservação da biodiversidade e o desenvolvimento sustentável em ambos os países", acrescentou ele. Essa cooperação também está se estendendo aos parceiros da Iniciativa Cinturão e Rota. Muitos deles estão implementando ativamente políticas verdes e sustentáveis, ao mesmo tempo que mobilizam capital. "A China adaptou serviços para diferentes regiões, incluindo a promoção da aplicação de instrumentos de finanças verdes e do desenvolvimento de mercado, a realização de pesquisas aprofundadas sobre políticas verdes e o avanço dos mecanismos do mercado de carbono", disse Cheng Lin, chefe do Escritório do Secretariado em Beijing para os Princípios de Investimento Verde para a Iniciativa Cinturão e Rota. Especialistas observaram na conferência que, como as tecnologias digitais e inteligentes remodelaram profundamente o setor financeiro nos últimos anos, potencializar as finanças verdes com essas tecnologias é um caminho fundamental para o desenvolvimento sustentável global. "As tecnologias digitais e inteligentes podem oferecer um importante apoio às finanças verdes, superando gargalos na coleta e análise de dados e monitoramento e avaliação de riscos", disse Zhang Bei, vice-chefe do departamento de pesquisa do Banco Popular da China. À medida que os eventos climáticos extremos se tornam mais frequentes, tecnologias como sistemas de informação geográfica, sensoriamento remoto por satélite e grandes modelos de linguagem podem ajudar a avaliar com maior precisão como diferentes regiões e grupos populacionais estão lidando com as mudanças climáticas, identificar prioridades para a adaptação e direcionar o financiamento para as áreas com maiores necessidades, observou Zhang. O papel cada vez mais importante da tecnologia digital nas finanças verdes da China deve beneficiar mais parceiros globais em seus esforços de desenvolvimento sustentável. Mari Elka Pangestu, vice-presidente do Conselho Econômico Nacional da Indonésia, disse que a China é líder em tecnologias limpas. Ela expressou esperança de aprofundar a cooperação com parceiros chineses além do investimento de capital, por meio do estabelecimento de mais joint ventures, do aumento da produção local e do fortalecimento da transferência de tecnologia. O 15º Plano Quinquenal da China (2026-2030) prevê a expansão de produtos e serviços financeiros verdes e o incentivo a maiores investimentos no desenvolvimento verde e de baixo carbono.

artigo.texto: The San Diego City Council today is expected to approve Mayor Todd Gloria’s proposed temporary ban on large data centers Tuesday, but it likely would do almost nothing to stop a potential data center near the Midway District that developers have been exploring. Our MacKenzie Elmer recently broke the news about a 400-megawatt data center that Manchester Financial Group has considered building on U.S Navy land. If built, it could possibly be the largest data center in all of California. Because it’s federal land, the Council is essentially powerless. But it’s not just that. President Trump is encouraging data centers. He has ordered the Secretary of War to identify military sites that could house large-scale data centers, like the one proposed. At today’s meeting, councilmembers will vote on whether to put an emergency ordinance in place that would pause all pending applications for data centers for 45 days. The Council can keep renewing the ban for a total of 20 months. The goal is to use that time to come up with regulations for how data centers might fit within city zoning. Gloria said at an event last week that without new regulations, it would be almost as easy to permit a data center as a warehouse. Supe Candidate Clarifies Where He Stands on County Sales Tax District 5 Supervisor candidate Kyle Krahel is trying to set the record straight about his stance on Measure B, a proposed countywide half-cent sales tax increase on this year’s ballot. At our Politifest North County even this month he took a bold and very clear position in support of it, but the Union-Tribune reports that he said he was opposed to the measure six months ago. Krahel told our Tigist Layne it was all a misunderstanding. Krahel is a Democrat running against Republican Rebecca Jones, who is the mayor of San Marcos, to serve on the county Board of Supervisors. Krahel didn’t stutter at Politifest when he said “people are going to die on our streets” if Measure B fails, explaining that it will be difficult to provide essential services to the region’s most vulnerable people without that extra revenue. That’s because the federal government has been rolling out massive cuts to food benefits, health care coverage and many safety-net programs as part of its “Big Beautiful Bill.” During an online candidate forum in April, Krahel said he was opposed to Measure B. But he told Voice that wasn’t the case. He thought the moderator had asked each candidate if they generally support sales tax increases, and his answer was no. But when it comes to Measure B, he said, he was in support of it then and still is today. “I am generally skeptical of any tax increase, especially regressive taxes like sales taxes, partly because it hurts working families,” Krahel said. “I didn’t realize that it was that specific question. artigo.texto: ANEEL has approved the final rules for Brazil’s large-scale battery storage auctions EPE registered 6,091 projects with close to 300 GW capacity across the two auctions in August 2026 Winning projects will secure 15-year contracts starting from August 2028 Brazil’s energy regulator, the National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL), has approved the final rules for the country’s first large-scale battery energy storage auctions scheduled to be held on December 2 and 4, 2026. The auctions will procure power availability from standalone battery energy storage systems (BESS) with contracts starting from August 1, 2028, and running for 15 years. The first auction, under Tender Notice No. 05/2026, requires equipment to meet domestic content criteria and minimum technical requirements dubbed National Storage category. Tender Notice No. 06/2026, under the Storage category, covers eligible projects for the second auction without the same domestic content requirement. Successful projects must be able to deliver their contracted maximum power for four hours/cycle, for up to two cycles a day, and a maximum of 366 cycles a year. The systems must also be capable of recharging fully within six hours. Both the auctions will contract power availability in MWs. Payments will be based on fixed annual revenue, paid in 12 monthly installments. The amount may be reduced depending on operational performance. ANEEL has also lowered the reference investment cost used to calculate financial guarantees, from BRL 9.8 million/MW to BRL 6 million/MW. The agency said this would reduce entry barriers and encourage competition. These plans follow the Ministry of Mines and Energy launching a public consultation for the auctions as part of the 2026 Reserve Capacity Auction (LRCAP)—Storage in November 2025 as part of Brazil’s efforts to secure grid stability and affordable tariffs (see Brazil Announces Country’s Maiden Battery Storage Systems Auction). In August 2026, the Energy Research Office (EPE) completed the registration process for projects interested in participating in the LRCAP auctions. It registered a total of 6,091 projects representing 296.8 GW of power capacity. Brazil’s solar energy association, ABSOLAR, has reportedly proposed a storage target of at least 8 GW by 2030 to be able to take advantage of renewable energy expansion and prepare the grid for the energy transition.

artigo.texto: What to Do About the Coming Glut of AI Data Centers Mark MacCarthy / Oct 27, 2026 There is a current shortage of AI data centers, but that shortage is temporary. More AI data centers will be built than will be needed to satisfy future AI compute demand. The industry is in the throes of a familiar bubble, where more investment flows into constructing facilities for a new technology than can be supported by customer demand. This has happened before with railroads and internet communications facilities and is happening again now with AI data centers. An oversupply is usually followed by a contraction — prices and supply collapse until an equilibrium is restored. But in this case the overexpansion of AI data centers is so large that the contraction is likely to have substantial macroeconomic consequences, a rapid decline in stock values and economic activity across the economy. This sequence of a recession following an overexpansion is also a familiar pattern established by the earlier overexpansion of railroads and internet facilities. Regulation can serve several purposes other than preventing the coming AI data center crash. Policymakers generally know how to protect electricity ratepayers from paying the costs of providing service to AI data centers and picking up the bill for stranded transmission and distribution facilities no longer needed to supply AI data centers. Policymakers are moving toward AI safety regulation needed to protect against dangerous AI experiments by AI developers. Congress should begin a series of hearings on the liability of AI developers and deployers for damages caused by AI models and agents, and a system of insurance needed to make sure victims of these mishaps can be compensated. Policymakers must also begin to address inaccuracies and unreliability of AI models, especially in consequential areas such as providing health information to the public. Along with collaborators, I will be addressing these issues in upcoming commentaries. Unfortunately, the system of governance in the US does not provide policy tools to prevent the coming oversupply-contraction cycle in AI data centers. Generally speaking investors are free to put their money where they feel they can earn the largest return, even if the collective result is an economic crash. Policymakers should be aware, however, of the industry dynamics that are leading to this outcome, even if there is little they can do to stop it. AI data centers today and tomorrow Chips are the key physical elements in an AI data center. Strung together in elaborate layouts of ever-increasing density within enormous physical structures, they are the devices that AI companies use to train and operate their AI models. There are shortages of chips, especially memory chips, and prices for these scarce items are soaring. But the major cloud computing companies, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have been able to secure a steady supply of chips from providers like Nvidia and have begun to develop chips of their own. In addition to chips, data centers costs include land, design and engineering expenses, construction of physical structures, power, cooling facilities, and networking expenses. Together with Meta, the three major cloud companies are expected to devote roughly $750 billion to capital expenditures this year alone, almost all of it focused on these AI infrastructure expenses. Often independent developers build and operate data centers specifically designed to handle AI workloads and lease them to cloud computing tenants or directly to AI developers. One of these “neocloud” providers, CoreWeave, for example, has Microsoft, OpenAI and Meta as leading customers. The leading AI companies, including Anthropic and OpenAI, have been scrambling to secure adequate compute through contracts with companies operating data centers and providing chips. Anthropic said it expects to spend at least $518 billion over the coming decade building AI infrastructure with six partners including the big three cloud computing companies, Google, Microsoft and Amazon, according to a confidential IPO prospectus. Including chip deals with companies like Broadcom means that Anthropic’s future AI infrastructure costs top $600 billion, according to its draft S1 prospectus, a figure confirmed by the formal release of its prospectus on October 26. There is a widely recognized shortfall in current data center capacity. As Wall Street Journal reporter Asa Fitch noted, “A data-center crunch is coming.” According to a recent Morgan Stanley analysis, estimated global demand for data center capacity will be “about 56 gigawatts next year, with just 51 gigawatts of new facilities being energized.” In 2028, estimated demand climbs to 86 gigawatts, but “only 68 gigawatts of computing power come online.” Protests against data centers have the potential to slow data center expansion to meet this unmet demand. Texas and New York have halted the construction of new AI data centers and Pennsylvania and Oregon have imposed new limits. Heatmap reports the “cancellation” of $260 billion worth of data center projects in 2026. Some of this is a healthy shakeout. Utilities have known for some time about “phantom” data centers, where companies operating data centers ask utilities for power they might not need, sometimes because they file the same energy requests with several utilities at the same time. But new requirements on potential data center customers have begun to purge utility wait lists of phantom data centers. Despite protests and moratoria, data center expansion still seems to be on track. The industry analysis firm, Semianalysis, estimates that data center capacity will double in 2027 compared with 2026. The ultimate driver of this demand for AI data centers is increasing usage of AI services, mostly by enterprises, but also by individual users. By one estimate consumer AI spending has reached $40 billion this year, more than triple what it was a year ago. Anthropic’s AI

artigo.texto: Absolar vê data centers como solução para curtailment Entidade cobra do presidente reeleito Lula a regulamentação do Redata e investimentos nas redes elétricas para viabilizar novos projetos no Brasil A Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (ABSOLAR) defendeu a atração de data centers como parte da solução para aproveitar a energia renovável cuja geração é cortada (curtailment) no Brasil. Em posicionamento divulgado após a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a entidade cobra do presidente reeleito a regulamentação do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), planejamento energético e investimentos nas redes de transmissão e distribuição. Segundo a associação, 17,2% do potencial de geração solar e eólica do País foi cortado no primeiro trimestre de 2026. A ABSOLAR relaciona esses cortes à falta de demanda e de capacidade de armazenamento da eletricidade disponível. Na avaliação da entidade, a instalação de data centers pode trazer novas cargas capazes de consumir parte dessa energia. A manifestação ocorre após Lula mencionar as fontes renováveis como um dos fatores para atrair investimentos em infraestrutura digital no discurso da vitória. “O Brasil reúne condições privilegiadas para transformar sua matriz renovável em vantagem competitiva, inclusive na atração de data centers, indústrias eletrointensivas, fábricas de hidrogênio verde e eletromobilidade”, afirma Rodrigo Sauaia, CEO da ABSOLAR. Redata e infraestrutura elétrica A associação aponta a regulamentação do Redata como uma das medidas necessárias para avançar nessa agenda. O regime prevê contrapartidas relacionadas ao uso de energia renovável ou de baixa emissão e depende de regulamentação do Poder Executivo para produzir efeitos. A entidade também ressalta que a atração de empreendimentos precisa ser acompanhada de planejamento energético e de expansão das redes elétricas. Segundo a ABSOLAR, a infraestrutura de transmissão e distribuição está entre os gargalos relatados por grandes consumidores que avaliam investimentos no Brasil. Data centers integram uma das três propostas apresentadas pela associação ao governo federal, aos governadores e ao Congresso Nacional para o período de 2027 a 2030. Batizada de “Energia que Emprega”, a iniciativa reúne ainda indústria eletrointensiva de baixo carbono, hidrogênio verde, eletrificação, eletromobilidade e planejamento da transmissão. A entidade associa esse conjunto de medidas à viabilização de 18 gigawatts (GW) em novas usinas solares. Leilões de baterias No curto prazo, a ABSOLAR considera os dois primeiros leilões de reserva de capacidade para contratação de sistemas de baterias, previstos no comunicado para 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026, o primeiro teste da agenda energética após as eleições. A associação pede definição das condições de custeio dos certames e defende contratações anuais de armazenamento. Na avaliação da entidade, as baterias podem dar flexibilidade ao sistema elétrico, mitigar os cortes de geração renovável e reduzir a necessidade de acionamento de termelétricas. A presidente do Conselho de Administração da ABSOLAR, Bárbara Rubim, também cobra previsibilidade regulatória e ressarcimento aos empreendimentos que tiveram a geração cortada. Entre as reivindicações estão incentivos para projetos de armazenamento, um marco legal próprio para a atividade e redução da carga tributária sobre baterias, que, segundo a associação, chega a 84,8%.
