artigo.texto: From Inverters to Full-Scenario Energy Storage: A Guide to SolisStorage's Product Portfolio Press Release Date 10-27-2026 Product highlights and application coverage across the energy storage portfolio CALIFORNIA, CA, UNITED STATES, October 27, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- In the solar industry, Ginlong (Solis) Technologies is a name that needs little introduction. Founded in 2005 in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2019 (stock code 300763), the company has spent two decades in power electronics. Its inverter products have evolved through seven generations of technology, it has been named a "Top Inverter Brand" by EuPD Research for 11 consecutive years, its products are sold in more than 100 countries and regions, and its annual production capacity has reached 80 GW. What deserves closer attention today, however, is the board Solis has been laying out around its energy storage subsidiary, SolisStorage: in-house development of PCS, EMS and system integration technologies, a product range covering residential, commercial and industrial (C&I), and grid-scale applications, and Solis AI tying the hardware to electricity markets. This article walks through that portfolio from a product and brand perspective. Residential Storage: The FlexAIO Flagship Residential is the product line closest to end users, and its flagship is the FlexAIO all-in-one stackable high-voltage energy storage system. Its design logic revolves around two words: flexibility and reliability. 6 kWh and 9 kWh battery packs can be mixed, as can old and new batteries; a single cluster stacks up to 6 modules, up to 6 clusters can run in parallel, and capacity scales all the way to 324 kWh — so the system grows as the household does. Reliability is engineered in finer detail: A+ grade cells with a cycle life of more than 10,000 cycles, five-layer hardware redundancy protection as standard, and continued safe operation of the whole system even if a single battery pack fails. On performance, FlexAIO supports 200% PV oversizing to raise generation utilization, switches seamlessly between on-grid and off-grid in under 10 milliseconds, and handles 150% overload for 10 seconds in off-grid mode. Built for outdoor installation, it carries IP66 protection and C5-M anti-corrosion, and with battery heating and active cooling its intelligent thermal management keeps it operating from -20°C to 55°C. Installation takes as little as 5 minutes, and ongoing maintenance is handled through OTA remote upgrades. The product has also stood up to third-party scrutiny: in October 2026, FlexAIO received IEC 62619 and IEC 63056 IECEE CB certificates from TÜV Rheinland — the former covering industrial lithium battery safety, the latter covering safety requirements for residential energy storage systems. Through the CB scheme's mutual recognition framework, these two certificates clear compliance hurdles for market entry across multiple countries and regions. C&I Storage: The EverCore ESS Platform Approach C&I is the fastest-growing part of Solis' storage business. The first 50 kW hybrid storage inverters shipped in July 2025, the 125 kW model followed in December of the same year, and by October 2026 cumulative global shipments across the full 50–125 kW range had passed 3 GW — in under 16 months. Behind that growth lies the sheer diversity of C&I demand: some customers want to use more of their own solar generation, some need to manage peak demand, some prioritize backup power, and electricity market rules and project conditions vary widely from place to place. Kun Zhang, Product Center Director at Solis, puts it plainly: "Different markets require different power levels, system configurations and operating strategies. Our approach is to build a versatile product platform with a high level of adaptability." That platform approach is embodied in the EverCore Energy Storage System (ESS). It offers three cabinet capacities — 100.48 kWh, 120.57 kWh and 261.24 kWh — and can be paired with 30–75 kW inverters (for low-voltage grids) and 50–125 kW inverters (for standard-voltage grids). Under its AC-DC separation architecture, a single inverter can connect up to 6 battery cabinets in parallel, so capacity can be expanded without additional inverter investment. The 125 kW all-in-one model integrates PCS, STS, PV inverter, circuit-breaker protection and EMS into one unit, achieving seamless on-grid/off-grid switching in under 10 milliseconds without an external STS, while supporting both DC and AC coupling and 200% PV oversizing. Thermal management and safety are the baseline for cabinet-type storage. EverCore stays with air cooling, using a three-air-duct architecture that combines a patented diversion air duct with Coanda-effect airflow to improve heat dissipation efficiency by roughly 30% over conventional air cooling. It is designed to operate from -25°C to 55°C at altitudes up to 4,000 meters. On the safety side, EVE 314Ah cells (8,000 cycles at 0.5C, 70% capacity retention, internal resistance as low as 0.15±0.05 mΩ) are paired with a 15-layer protective system — including thermal insulation between packs able to withstand 1,000°C, and a three-stage fire-suppression mechanism of pack-level aerosol, cabinet-level aerosol and fire-fighting water channels. Further up the scale, EverCore units can be paralleled to 1.25 MW, reaching grid-scale applications such as peak shaving and frequency regulation. These products cover C&I scenarios ranging from factories and farms to shopping malls, hospitals and large residences. Where site space is limited, the modular FlexCore-ID (indoor) and FlexCore-OD (outdoor) are the alternatives — the former built around 20 kWh battery packs and 314Ah LFP cells, the latter designed for direct outdoor deployment. artigo.texto: Alton residents pack open house about possible data center at former steel mill Developer Terrawatt has not yet submitted a proposal to the city ALTON, Ill. (First Alert 4) - Dozens of Alton residents attended an open house to learn about a possible data center at the former Alton Steel Mill. The project from developer Terrawatt is drawing mixed reactions. The line to get into the open house wrapped around the block, with many people waiting 45 minutes to an hour. Inside, the room was packed, with representatives speaking about the project. Protesters held up signs and banners, voicing their opposition. Residents share concerns and support Stacy Roquemore, who lives in Alton, said he is concerned about the project. “The noise, the pollution, it’s everything, the raising of costs of our bills and I mean as everyone knows here in Illinois, the costs of our electric, gas and water are already so high,” Roquemore said. Some attendees said they believe the project will bring opportunity. Russell Scott, a Local 218 union worker, said he supports it. “It helps the brothers and sisters out with more jobs and stuff like that. Just more jobs, that’s all,” Scott said. Steven Landreth, a local electrician who lives in Alton, also said he sees a benefit. “The city needs a place to bring in some cash, some local business and jobs,” Landreth said. Other attendees said they are keeping an open mind. One attendee said he wants to hear details about the project. “I just want to hear the time frame, and then what they say the impact is going to be on the public, what they will do to local power, the local water…” the attendee said. Christy Fritz-Parker, a homeowner in Alton, said she opposes the project. She was among several protestors who stayed outside the open house. “I think they were hoping that here in Alton, we’re maybe not as educated as maybe St. Louis or these other communities, but I want them to know that the word is out and people here in Alton do not want the data center,” Fritz-Parker said. Development consultant says project will benefit Alton Cecilia Dvorak, CEO of Steadfast City Economic and Community Partners, is from the development consultant firm working with Terrawatt. She said the open house provides a venue for people to learn about the proposal and its impacts. “We’re able to provide a venue for people to get a little bit of understanding of the proposal itself, also the impacts. And then the conversation also helps us inform what the proposal looks like,” Dvorak said. Dvorak said the project will be beneficial for Alton. “There’s a significant amount of benefit, particularly in tax revenues that can be generated by the project just by its presence,” Dvorak said. Project details and next steps The proposed data center would be called the Riverbend Technology Center. It would be housed at the former Alton Steel Mill, which closed at the start of the year. Some residents also expressed concern about Terrawatt because the company is behind the data center project at the Armory in Midtown St. Louis. Terrawatt sued the city several months ago over prerequisites for construction. Terrawatt has not yet submitted a proposal to the city of Alton on the data center. Reporter Raya Torres was told the goal is to submit the proposal by the end of the year, but that is not definite. The company said it was important to host the open house so it could inform people about its proposal. Copyright 2026 KMOV. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: O Rio Grande do Norte vai receber o segundo Data Center do Sistema Sebrae no Brasil. A estrutura será inaugurada nesta quinta-feira (29), às 18h30, na sede do Sebrae-RN, em Natal, e ficará responsável pelo armazenamento e processamento de dados de unidades da instituição em 12 estados das regiões Nordeste, Norte e Sudeste. O investimento previsto é de aproximadamente R$ 70 milhões. Os recursos são provenientes do Sebrae Nacional e das unidades estaduais que utilizarão o equipamento. Com a inauguração, o Rio Grande do Norte passará a contar com uma estrutura desse tipo no sistema, ao lado do Distrito Federal, onde funciona o primeiro Data Center da instituição. O espaço receberá o nome de Senador Fernando Bezerra, que foi o primeiro presidente do Conselho Deliberativo do Sebrae-RN, na década de 1990. Ele também participou da viabilização da compra do imóvel onde funciona a atual sede da instituição, na capital potiguar. Segundo Franklin Maux, gerente de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação do Sebrae-RN, a escolha do estado levou em consideração, entre outros fatores, o potencial energético potiguar. A disponibilidade de fontes renováveis pode favorecer a instalação de empreendimentos de infraestrutura tecnológica. A nova estrutura também deve permitir maior padronização dos sistemas utilizados pelas unidades estaduais, que atualmente operam com diferentes tecnologias. De acordo com o Sebrae-RN, o projeto poderá estimular investimentos no setor de tecnologia no estado e contribuir para a formação de profissionais especializados. Um Data Center é uma instalação que concentra servidores, equipamentos de rede e sistemas de armazenamento responsáveis pelo processamento, gerenciamento e proteção de informações. A estrutura será utilizada para atender às operações das unidades do Sebrae contempladas pelo projeto.

artigo.texto: [SMM Cobalt Morning Meeting Summary] Raw material prices continue to decline, end-use demand is weak, and the market is under pressure At the start of this week, the industry chain remained in the doldrums overall, with raw material prices continuing to slide, end-use demand weak, and market purchasing sentiment cautious. Electrolytic metal prices temporarily stabilised, consolidating around 230,000 yuan/mt, with low imports and production cut rumours boosting market confidence, though supply-demand fundamentals had yet to improve. Sulphate prices continued to pull back, with some traders quoting close to 40,000 yuan/mt, and lower recycled raw material costs further weakened price support. Chloride and trimanganese tetroxide prices weakened in tandem, with downstream inventory high and purchasing demand insufficient. Actual transactions for metal powder fell to around 275,000 yuan/mt, and the market still faced downward pressure. The cathode material segment remained under pressure, with ternary cathode precursor processing coefficients weakening and operating rates declining at some enterprises; ternary cathode material order growth was sluggish, and November production schedules were expected to decline further. Consumer cathode materials were dragged down by sluggish end-use demand and falling raw material prices, prompting enterprises to proactively cut production, while inventory destocking remained slow. On the industry news front, XTC New Energy Materials (Xiamen) plans to invest 723 million yuan to build a project with annual capacity of 40,000 mt of LFP; GSP Automotive Group's solid-liquid hybrid battery production line debugging fell short of expectations. Overall, the market is expected to consolidate on a weak note in the near term, with price stabilisation contingent on demand recovery and inventory digestion.

artigo.texto: Financing battery energy storage: key legal considerations for investors and lenders At a glance Developers typically finance battery energy storage systems (BESS) through non-recourse project finance structures using an SPV. Their volatile, market-driven reve-nues set them apart from wind and solar projects. A BESS project’s bankability depends on its revenue model. Tolling agreements offer the greatest financing certainty, while fully merchant projects require significantly more equity and face stricter covenants. The regulatory framework affects project economics and requires legal assessment early in project development. A largely unrestricted grid connection, or at least a grid connection commitment, is fundamental to any BESS project. Equity is a key component of bankable BESS financings. Investors may earn higher returns, but they also bear greater risks, particularly because they rank behind lend-ers and depend on volatile revenues. Battery energy storage systems (BESS) rank among the key technologies of the energy transition. They add flexibility to the power system, help integrate renewable energy and open up new trading opportunities – from balancing energy through arbitrage to ancillary services. Financing them nonetheless remains challenging: unlike wind and solar projects, they lack long-term guaranteed remuneration. Revenues are volatile, market-based and hard to forecast. Whether a battery storage system proves bankable therefore also depends on how it is structured legally. I. Financing structures: project finance and the non-recourse principle BESS projects are typically structured as standalone project financings through a special purpose vehicle (SPV). The financing follows the non-recourse principle: lenders have no recourse to the shareholders and rely instead solely on the project’s cash flows and assets. Typical loan tenors run between seven and ten years. The crucial difference from conventional renewable energy financing lies in the revenue profile. Where wind and solar projects often build on long-term feed-in tariffs, BESS revenues track dynamic market prices. That drives higher equity requirements, more conservative valuations and shorter loan tenors. Typical features of the financing documentation for BESS projects include: - Sculpted repayment matched to the batteries’ degradation curve - DSCR covenants - Cash-sweep mechanisms and restricted-payment clauses - Augmentation reserves funding later capacity additions The security package typically includes a pledge over the shares in the SPV, an all-assets assignment of claims under the material project agreements, pledges over bank accounts and a transfer of title to the facility by way of security. The last of these matters especially because batteries count as movable assets so lenders cannot take a mortgage over them. Securing rights in rem over a site is all the more important: without robust land, access and cable rights (usually secured through first-ranking limited personal easements in favour of the SPV and the lenders) financing cannot be structured. Reviewing site security is therefore a standard part of legal due diligence and deserves early attention, given how much it can delay a project. II. Revenue models and bankability A BESS project’s revenues typically rest on three pillars: ancillary services (notably FCR and aFRR), peak shaving and avoided network charges, and wholesale arbitrage. In practice projects combine these sources through revenue stacking. Prequalification requirements, state-of-charge management and technical constraints, however, limit how far they can do so. The choice of revenue model decides whether a project is bankable: - Tolling agreements offer the greatest planning certainty: the project company makes its storage capacity available to a counterparty and receives a fixed or partly variable fee. - Fully merchant projects are in principle bankable, but lenders apply significantly stricter requirements: they limit gearing more tightly, require higher DSCRs and additional liquidity reserves, and expect developers to update their trading forecasts regularly. - Hybrid floor structures strike a middle path, with loan-to-cost (LTC) ratios of 55–65%, for example through optimisation contracts with minimum fees. Degradation is a factor that should not be underestimated: batteries lose roughly 2-3% of their usable capacity each year. The financial model should realistically reflect this technical risk, which should be mitigated through manufacturer warranties and an augmentation reserve. Beyond that, bankability requires technical due diligence, an independent revenue forecast, qualified project partners and confirmation that the project can obtain insurance. III. Regulatory framework The regulatory framework significantly affects a BESS project’s economics so developers must factor it into project development at an early stage. Grid connection: A grid connection is fundamental to financing any BESS project. Transmission system operators and, increasingly, distribution system operators use maturity-based procedures to allocate grid capacity. Developers should clarify availability, connection capacity, costs and deadlines early. Flexible connection arrangements can make it easier to connect a project, but they may restrict how the project can operate. The grid connection contribution also represents a material investment and site-selection factor, as reflected in recent Federal Court of Justice case law (2025). Exemption from network charges: Battery storage currently benefits from an exemption from network charges if it enters operation by 4 August 2029. The statutory deadline for new storage projects to qualify ends on that date. artigo.texto: RES has welcomed its first consent for a battery energy storage system (BESS) in Northern Ireland, after Mid and East Antrim Borough Council’s Planning Committee approved the Ballyross BESS. Located on land approximately 2 km south-west of Gleno and 8.5 km south-west of Larne, Ballyross is strategically positioned close to the existing Ballyvallagh substation. This will support the efficient operation of the system while minimising the need for additional grid infrastructure. As constraints on Northern Ireland's electricity system increase, clean, low-cost electricity capable of powering homes and businesses can sometimes be prevented from reaching consumers. Battery energy storage projects such as Ballyross can help make better use of this electricity by storing it when generation is high and releasing it when demand rises. By adding flexibility and supporting grid stability, Ballyross will help create a more efficient and resilient electricity system. Peter Deeney, Senior Development Project Manager at RES, said: "From our office in Larne, RES has been proud to contribute to Northern Ireland’s energy future and economic growth since the early 1990s. Securing consent for Ballyross, our first battery energy storage project to be consented in Northern Ireland, is an important milestone as we continue transforming the way energy is generated, stored, and supplied. “Battery storage is becoming increasingly important as Northern Ireland continues its transition to a low-carbon energy system. Projects such as Ballyross can help make the electricity network more flexible and resilient, so that more renewable energy can be stored and used when it is needed most.” The approved scheme also includes a substantial landscaping package. New native-species planting will help the development blend into the surrounding landscape while creating wildlife corridors and pollinator-friendly habitat that deliver additional biodiversity benefits. Peter continued: “Alongside its strategic location close to Ballyvallagh substation, the site was selected because it has limited visibility from local properties. The new planting will further reduce visibility while providing valuable resources for a wide range of flora and fauna. “We would particularly like to thank the local residents and stakeholders who engaged with us throughout the development of Ballyross. The feedback shared during consultation helped inform our landscaping plan and shape the project’s final design.” For more news and technical articles from the global renewable industry, read the latest issue of Energy Global magazine. artigo.texto: Third-quarter profit growth slowed to 14.5%, fueled by competition from secondary manufacturers. According to the unaudited financial report submitted to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on October 20, 2026, Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL) recorded operating revenue of 165.22 billion yuan (approximately US$24.74 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, a 58.58% increase year-on-year. Net profit attributable to parent company shareholders reached 21.25 billion yuan (approximately US$3.18 billion), a 14.54% increase compared to the third quarter of 2025. The gross profit margin for the period declined to 19.3%. Despite maintaining positive year-on-year growth, CATL's net profit growth rate in Q3 2026 slowed significantly compared to the 36% increase in Q2 2026 and the 57% increase recorded in Q4 2025. Simultaneously, both revenue and net profit figures for the past quarter were lower than the average forecast of analysts, which were RMB 175.05 billion in revenue and RMB 26.03 billion in net profit. Immediately after the financial results were released, CATL's stock fell by more than 10% on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and 8.6% on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange during this week's trading sessions. The stock's decline has continued since September 2026, following the signing of supply agreements between domestic electric vehicle manufacturers Xiaomi and Li Auto and secondary battery producers. Besides market share competition, investor caution regarding the outlook for energy storage systems has also contributed to selling pressure, causing CATL's share price to fall by more than 20% on the Hong Kong market and 31% on the Shenzhen market since the beginning of 2026. For the first nine months of 2026, CATL's total operating revenue reached 442.14 billion yuan (approximately US$66.19 billion), a 56% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Net profit for the nine months reached 64.53 billion yuan (approximately US$9.66 billion), a 32% increase year-on-year. Research and development (R&D) expenses for the first three quarters were recorded at 18.52 billion yuan. Inventories rose 53% to over 144 billion yuan amid forecasts of slowing global battery demand in 2027. Amidst volatility in profit margins within China's electric vehicle industry, investment bank JPMorgan downgraded its Hong Kong-listed CATL stock rating to Neutral earlier this week. JPMorgan's report indicated that the re-imposition of consumption tax on battery products, the rollback of export tax refunds, and international trade barriers are creating significant costs for Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers, potentially dampening demand for CATL's battery products. However, the financial institution still believes CATL will maintain its leading position in terms of scale within the global battery industry. Sharing a cautious view on market prospects, in a report published in early October 2026, Citigroup forecasts that the growth rate of global battery consumption demand will decrease by 26% in 2027. This is due to the shrinking growth potential of the domestic electric vehicle market in China, combined with the slowdown in the energy storage system sector due to the high base level of the previous period. Regarding asset size and production expansion, as of September 30, 2026, CATL's inventory value reached 144.77 billion yuan (equivalent to US$21.68 billion), a 53% increase compared to the beginning of the year. The value of the group's ongoing infrastructure projects also increased by 45%, reaching 43 billion yuan (equivalent to US$6.44 billion). Company representatives explained that the increase in inventory and ongoing project costs was to support the plan to expand factory scale and enhance production capacity in the coming period. To support liquidity and stabilize stock prices on the stock market, earlier this week, CATL spent nearly 50 million yuan (approximately $7.49 million) to repurchase treasury shares listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. This transaction is part of the largest share buyback program in the company's history, with a total registered value of up to 40 billion yuan (equivalent to $6 billion) on the mainland stock market, announced in July 2026.

artigo.texto: A empresa de Elon Musk fechou um acordo de financiamento de 40 bilhões de dólares com a Apollo Global Management. O objetivo é comprar e alugar equipamentos de alta performance, como chips gráficos, para operar seus próprios centros de dados, com pagamentos ao longo de cinco anos. A SpaceX, a empresa espacial liderada pelo bilionário Elon Musk, acertou um acordo de financiamento no valor de cerca de 40 bilhões de dólares. O parceiro escolhido foi uma entidade administrada pela Apollo Global Management. O principal objetivo da operação é adquirir equipamentos avançados para a construção e operação de centros de dados próprios. Conforme documento oficial enviado nesta segunda-feira, 26, à Securities and Exchanges Commission (SEC), órgão regulador de mercados dos Estados Unidos, a transação prevê a compra de unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) e outros itens relacionados. A estratégia visa fortalecer a infraestrutura tecnológica da empresa para suportar operações de inteligência artificial e computação pesada. Detalhes do acordo e cronograma - O compromisso legal entre as partes foi assinado no dia 24 de outubro. - A entidade ligada à Apollo será responsável por comprar os equipamentos. - Depois, esses itens serão alugados pela Apollo para a SpaceX. - A SpaceX pagará valores trimestrais pela utilização da infraestrutura. - O período total dos contratos de arrendamento é de aproximadamente cinco anos. Como funcionará a entrega e o pagamento Os equipamentos não chegarão de uma só vez. A entrega ocorrerá em lotes distintos, seguindo um cronograma estabelecido. Os contratos individuais de aluguel estão previstos para começar a valer no primeiro semestre de 2027. Cada contrato terá uma duração que varia entre cinco anos e cinco anos e três meses, dependendo do lote específico. Sobre a parte financeira, a SpaceX confirmou que os pagamentos trimestrais serão feitos de forma antecipada. Em geral, cada parcela incluirá um vigésimo (1/20) do custo financiado do lote correspondente. Além disso, será acrescido um valor de juros, calculado sobre o saldo devedor a uma taxa anual fixa, que ainda será definida, bem como despesas adicionais. Impacto financeiro e formalização Os cálculos da SpaceX estimam que os pagamentos referentes ao principal do empréstimo totalizem aproximadamente 40 bilhões de dólares durante a vigência dos contratos. Este valor, no entanto, não inclui o montante dos juros nem outros custos operacionais que possam surgir. A empresa espera concluir a formalização final do acordo antes do fim de 2026, dependendo do cumprimento de determinadas condições preliminares.

artigo.texto: The San Diego City Council, on a 9-0 vote Tuesday, passed an urgency ordinance that places a moratorium on the development of new data centers within the city. Coming days after an executive order from Mayor Todd Gloria, the moratorium is designed to give officials time to develop policies and recommendations to make sure that data centers align with the city’s General Plan and its Climate Action Plan. “I appreciate the City Council’s unanimous ratification of the temporary moratorium on data center development,” Gloria said in a statement. “This is a necessary and responsible step to make sure any development does not outpace our responsibility to protect San Diegans.” The temporary moratorium lasts 45 days but gives the City Council the power to extend the suspension for another 10 months and 15 days. No more than two extensions will be allowed and will require approval from four-fifths of the council. The pause “gives us time to start putting the right regulations in place,” Councilmember Marni von Wilpert said. “AI data centers must pay their own way without passing additional electricity or water costs onto our residents. It is already too expensive to live here.” The moratorium, however, does not figure to directly impact any possible construction of a data center that the Manchester Financial Group is exploring as part of its plans to redevelop the 70.3-acre Naval Base Point Loma Old Town Campus, which is home to Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR). That’s because NAVWAR is on federal land, beyond the city’s jurisdiction. Manchester Financial executives have looked at the possibility of a data center to make up a portion of the NAVWAR site, although the group says it is merely one of a range of options on the table. The current development plan already contemplates a number of definitive uses, including 8,900 residential units and two hotels totaling 480 rooms. The company has floated the idea of a 400-megawatt data center, which would be the largest in California, but Manchester president and CEO Ted Eldredge told the Union-Tribune last week, “We’re not married to that megawattage” and that any possible facility is dependent on market conditions and overall feasibility. After Tuesday’s vote, Eldredge said in a statement, “We continue to look at a variety of options for the site as we seek to build a best-in-class facility for the Navy,” adding that any proposed plans must go through environmental review before any decisions will be made. “The City and public will have (the) opportunity to review proposed plans and provide comment,” Eldredge said. “We remain committed to working with the Navy and community stakeholders throughout this process.” Essential toward driving the boom in artificial intelligence, data centers have drawn increasing scrutiny across the country in recent months. The facilities house racks of computer systems required to train generative AI models and chatbots. Supporters say data centers can drive cutting-edge technology and actually drive down overall energy costs through economies of scale. But critics worry the electricity needed to feed data centers will strain the grid and drive already steep power bills in San Diego Gas & Electric’s service territory — with rates at or the near the top of most expensive in the country — even higher. In addition, data centers, in order to stay cool, can suck up large amounts of water. The moratorium aims to set data center guidelines within the city’s purview. The pause passed Tuesday includes establishing a working group of as many as 15 stakeholders to develop recommendations for water and electricity demand and potential impacts on utility bills, housing and neighborhoods. “San Diego welcomes innovation, investment and the jobs that come with them,” Gloria said. “What we will not do is ask residents to absorb unnecessary costs or neighborhood impacts.” Councilmember Sean Elo-Rivera called for, and the City Council accepted, a list of principles to guide the framework for what the Gloria administration and city staff may permanently put into place. They include policies seeking “no direct or indirect costs to San Diego residents or ratepayers;” data centers that use 100% renewable energy and no fossil fuels for backup generation; a plan for using recycled water at the facilities; and a “minimum separation” distance between any data centers and schools, parks and child care facilities. “People want quick, decisive action on this, not a long bureaucratic conversation,” Elo-Rivera said. “People don’t want data centers in their communities and the reasons are loud and clear.” Though not formally included within the moratorium, Elo-Rivera called for SDG&E to be excluded from the city’s proposed stakeholder group of up to 15 members. “In SDG&E’s eyes, no cost to San Diegans has ever been excessive,” said Elo-Rivera, a frequent critic of the utility. “They remind us of that every single month, and now they want even more,” referring to an upcoming SDG&E general rate case before the California Public Utilities Commission. Asked for a reaction, SDG&E spokesperson Anthony Wagner told the Union-Tribune that a working group examining data center issues “should include the relevant technical expertise, including SDG&E. Our focus will remain on ensuring new large customers, not existing customers, pay the costs associated with connecting them to the grid.” Tuesday’s council hearing drew 70 speakers during the sometimes raucous public comment period (both in-person and via phone), with all the commenters expressing opposition to data center growth. “This moratorium is not an anti-technology stance,” San Diego resident Sean Tighe said. “It is essential to have an existing legal foundation for utility use and land use before considering the wrecking ball of a data center that voraciously consumes public resources.” Some called for a complete ban of all data centers within the city limits. “Don’t let this be the final st

artigo.texto: Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore), through its Energy Research Institute @ NTU (ERI@N), and Singapore energy storage company VFT have launched a S$15 million joint research laboratory to develop safer, more durable and cost-effective batteries for storing renewable electricity and supporting future power grids. The NTU-VFT Joint Lab was launched at the Asia Clean Energy Summit, held as part of Singapore International Energy Week 2026. Unlike lithium-ion batteries, which store energy within battery cells themselves, VRFBs store energy in liquid electrolytes held in external tanks. Because their storage capacity can be increased simply by using larger tanks, they are well suited to storing and supplying electricity over extended periods, making them a candidate technology for large-scale, long-duration energy storage. A key safety advantage of the technology lies in its chemistry. VRFBs use non-flammable, aqueous-based liquids to store energy, significantly reducing the risk of battery fires compared with conventional lithium-ion batteries. This characteristic is becoming increasingly relevant as power grids incorporate more intermittent renewable energy sources such as solar and wind, requiring storage systems that can absorb electricity when renewable generation is high and release it when needed, helping to maintain a reliable power supply. Professor Madhavi Srinivasan, Executive Director of ERI@N, said: “As the global energy transition accelerates, safe and efficient energy storage will become increasingly important to keeping electricity supplies stable and reliable. By combining NTU’s deep expertise in materials science, AI, energy technologies and sustainability with VFT’s industry experience, we aim to develop safer, longer-lasting and sustainable batteries to power our future energy grid.” She added that VFT’s journey shows how NTU’s research can translate into real-world applications, noting that what began as a spin-off from NTU working on their first generation of energy storage systems has evolved into a company developing commercial energy-storage systems, and expressing that the university is glad to be working with VFT once again to develop the next generation of energy storage solutions and drive further innovation. Dr Vidal Bharath, Chief Executive Officer of VFT, framed the challenge facing modern power systems: “The challenge is no longer simply generating more renewable energy. Power systems also need safe, reliable and affordable ways to store that electricity for use when renewable generation falls or demand rises.” He said that by combining NTU’s research capabilities with VFT’s experience in developing and deploying flow batteries, the partners aim to overcome the technical and cost barriers to wider adoption of new energy-storage technologies and accelerate commercial deployment. The research programme at the Joint Lab will pursue several technical directions. Researchers will develop more powerful and efficient flow batteries, including improved battery stacks and cooling systems designed to manage heat and boost performance. Other areas of research include improving power conversion and control systems to increase energy efficiency, and using artificial intelligence to monitor battery performance, detect faults and predict maintenance needs. Sustainability and cost are also central to the collaboration. The researchers will explore ways to recover and recycle vanadium from industrial waste and alternative sources, an approach that could potentially reduce costs and improve the sustainability of the technology. The S$15 million collaboration is supported under Singapore’s Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 plans and aims to develop new intellectual property, prototypes and technologies that can be progressively validated and incorporated into future commercial energy-storage systems. Beyond technology development, the Joint Lab is intended to strengthen Singapore’s talent and R&D capabilities in long-duration energy storage, helping the country transition towards cleaner and more resilient power systems. VFT, founded in 2018, is an NTU spin-off based on technology developed at ERI@N. The company raised US$20.5 million in 2025 to expand manufacturing and deployment of its flow-battery systems. The renewed partnership between the university and its spin-off reflects a broader effort to move laboratory-scale advances in energy storage toward commercial systems capable of supporting grids that increasingly depend on variable renewable generation. artigo.texto: O projeto de energia solar fotovoltaica em telhados, combinado com um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) na Zona Econômica de Vung Ang, é o primeiro projeto operado pela VinEnergo sob um contrato de compra de energia direta (DPPA). Os primeiros clientes a se beneficiarem da energia limpa e da tecnologia avançada de armazenamento de energia da VinEnergo são a Future Production, Investment and Development Joint Stock Company (proprietária e operadora da fábrica de carros e motocicletas elétricas VinFast em Ha Tinh) e a VinES Ha Tinh Energy Solutions Joint Stock Company (proprietária da fábrica de baterias VinES Ha Tinh). Além disso, o sistema solar fotovoltaico em telhados da VinEnergo também fornece eletricidade para a fábrica de baterias da joint venture VG, também localizada dentro do complexo de fabricação de baterias e veículos elétricos na Zona Econômica de Vung Ang. A VinEnergo opera um sistema de energia solar fotovoltaica em telhados, combinado com baterias de armazenamento de energia, em Ha Tinh. A VinEnergo Energy Joint Stock Company colocou oficialmente em operação um sistema de energia solar fotovoltaica em telhados, combinado com armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), para fornecer eletricidade limpa à fábrica de automóveis VinFast, à fábrica de baterias VinES e à joint venture de fabricação de baterias VG, na Zona Econômica de Vung Ang (província de Ha Tinh). Com uma capacidade total de até 22 MWp de energia solar e 45 MWh de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), a VinEnergo garante um fornecimento de energia estável a custos otimizados para seus parceiros, além de contribuir para a redução da sobrecarga na rede elétrica nacional. Segundo estimativas, em seu primeiro ano de operação, o sistema deverá gerar aproximadamente 39 milhões de kWh de energia limpa, contribuindo para a redução de mais de 25.000 toneladas de emissões de CO2 (o equivalente à absorção de mais de 1,13 milhão de árvores por ano). Em particular, a transição para a energia limpa da VinEnergo ajudará as unidades beneficiárias a reduzir a pressão sobre a rede elétrica e aumentar a autossuficiência energética, otimizando custos em cerca de 3,5 bilhões de VND por ano. O sucesso operacional e o fornecimento estável de energia às três usinas parceiras na fase inicial servem como base para que a VinEnergo continue desenvolvendo e promovendo a transição para energia verde nas fases subsequentes. Este modelo combina fontes de energia renováveis com um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) de grande escala, visando completar a infraestrutura de energia verde, a distribuição e a comercialização de eletricidade para os consumidores da região. A Sra. Nguyen Huong Giang, Vice-Diretora Geral da VinEnergo, declarou: “Por meio deste projeto, a VinEnergo irá gradualmente completar um ecossistema energético abrangente, desde fontes renováveis, sistemas de armazenamento e mecanismos de DPPA até infraestrutura de distribuição e varejo, capaz de atender à crescente demanda de eletricidade de projetos industriais emergentes na Zona Econômica de Vung Ang, em particular, e em todo o país, em geral. Temos orgulho de utilizar nossos próprios produtos, capacidades tecnológicas e plataforma de fabricação no Vietnã para solucionar os desafios energéticos de nossos parceiros comerciais, contribuindo para o aumento da competitividade e da participação de energia verde no setor industrial.” Atualmente, a VinEnergo fornece soluções de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) para diversos grandes projetos da Hanoi Power Corporation e da Northern Power Corporation, totalizando mais de 1,1 GWh, o que comprova a capacidade das empresas vietnamitas de dominar tecnologias essenciais e implementar projetos de grande escala. No mercado internacional, a VinEnergo anunciou um portfólio de projetos de energia renovável totalizando 10 GW e está atualmente implementando seus primeiros projetos na Ásia e na Europa. Nos próximos três anos, a VinEnergo pretende desenvolver um portfólio de projetos com capacidade total de até 100 GW, tornando-se assim uma das empresas líderes mundiais em energia renovável.

artigo.texto: Meio Ambiente Greenline leva tecnologia de carbono a fórum em Campo Grande Empresa brasileira participa de evento em 3 de novembro e reúne 14 projetos no Centro-Oeste, com potencial estimado de sequestrar 12,6 milhões de toneladas de CO₂ Uma empresa brasileira de tecnologia voltada ao monitoramento ambiental vai apresentar soluções para o mercado de carbono em Campo Grande. A Greenline participa, no dia 3 de novembro, do II Fórum MS Sustentabilidade, com iniciativas voltadas à conservação do Cerrado e do Pantanal. A atuação da companhia no Centro-Oeste reúne 14 projetos, que abrangem cerca de 134 mil hectares e têm potencial estimado de sequestro de 12,6 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono (CO₂), segundo dados divulgados pela empresa. O evento será realizado no Centro de Convenções Rubens Gil de Camillo e reunirá representantes de empresas, poder público, universidades e organizações da sociedade civil para discutir alternativas de desenvolvimento sustentável. Entre os temas da programação está o mercado de créditos de carbono. A Greenline desenvolve projetos com monitoramento digital que combina imagens de satélite, inteligência artificial e dados de vegetação. Segundo a empresa, a tecnologia permite acompanhar em tempo real toda a área das propriedades participantes. Os projetos e créditos emitidos passam por validação da certificadora independente Bureau Veritas, conforme informado pela companhia. Além da atuação regional, a empresa afirma desenvolver projetos que abrangem mais de 1,5 milhão de hectares no Brasil, com potencial estimado de geração de créditos equivalentes a mais de 25 milhões de toneladas de CO₂ por ano. A Greenline também integra um grupo de trabalho que discute metodologias para o mercado regulado de carbono no país. O fórum terá debates sobre recursos hídricos, agropecuária sustentável, energia, gestão de resíduos e economia regenerativa, com foco em soluções para os desafios ambientais e econômicos de Mato Grosso do Sul.

artigo.texto: EmissionLink pede alocação de receita do EU ETS para testes de captura de carbono marítima A EmissionLink, especialista em emissões do setor marítimo, defendeu que uma parcela dedicada das receitas do Sistema de Comércio de Emissões da União Europeia (EU ETS) seja direcionada a testes de captura de carbono a bordo e à infraestrutura portuária necessária para apoiá-los, segundo a empresa. A companhia alertou que, sem apoio financeiro direcionado, a tecnologia corre o risco de permanecer comercialmente inviável. Philippos Ioulianou, diretor-gerente da EmissionLink, sustenta que a Europa tem a oportunidade de acelerar o desenvolvimento da captura de carbono marítima ao canalizar as receitas do comércio de emissões para demonstrações em escala real. Na avaliação dele, esses projetos permitiriam estabelecer se a tecnologia é capaz de entregar reduções de emissões verificadas a um custo economicamente sustentável. O apelo surge enquanto a Organização Marítima Internacional (IMO) trabalha para desenvolver diretrizes de segurança interinas para sistemas de captura de carbono a bordo. Embora receba bem esse esforço, Ioulianou argumenta que o avanço regulatório precisa vir acompanhado de investimento em infraestrutura, em mecanismos de contabilização de emissões e em arranjos comerciais que tornem a tecnologia atrativa para os armadores. Segundo Ioulianou, diretrizes de segurança sozinhas não convencerão os armadores a investir em captura de carbono. Ele indicou que os proprietários exigem um caso de negócios crível, sustentado por economias de emissões verificadas, arranjos viáveis de descarte de carbono e uma visão clara dos benefícios financeiros. Acrescentou que a Europa está bem posicionada para liderar esse trabalho e que destinar parte das receitas do EU ETS a testes a bordo e à infraestrutura de recepção portuária ajudaria a determinar se a captura de carbono pode se tornar uma solução de descarbonização comercialmente viável para o transporte marítimo. A EmissionLink defende investimento em projetos de demonstração que abranjam todas as etapas do processo de captura de carbono, desde a coleta e o armazenamento a bordo até o desembarque, o transporte e o armazenamento permanente ou o uso aprovado. Segundo a empresa, esses projetos devem operar com base em critérios de desempenho claramente definidos e gerar dados de emissões verificáveis de forma independente, capazes de orientar o desenvolvimento regulatório e futuras decisões de investimento. A empresa adverte, porém, que a captura de carbono a bordo dificilmente se adequará a todas as embarcações. Navios em rotas fixas e previsíveis oferecem as aplicações iniciais mais promissoras, pois os operadores podem planejar a capacidade de armazenamento de carbono e organizar o desembarque em portos designados. Para embarcações em rotas irregulares ou em fretamentos spot, as dificuldades logísticas são consideravelmente maiores, sobretudo onde não há instalações de recepção de carbono nem transporte subsequente disponíveis. A adequação técnica também dependerá de fatores como a idade da embarcação, o espaço disponível, a demanda adicional de energia e a vida comercial remanescente. Armadores e afretadores precisam ainda resolver questões contratuais sobre o consumo extra de combustível, os atrasos no desembarque e a alocação dos benefícios de conformidade regulatória. Ioulianou explicou que a instalação de equipamentos de captura de carbono cria responsabilidades que vão muito além do investimento inicial. Segundo ele, os armadores precisam pesar o impacto operacional, as exigências impostas às tripulações e quem, em última instância, arca com os custos adicionais, e essas questões precisam de respostas antes que a tecnologia possa ser adotada com confiança. Outra preocupação é a necessidade de maior clareza sobre a contabilização de emissões e o reconhecimento regulatório. Embora o EU ETS reconheça a captura de carbono qualificada e o armazenamento geológico permanente ou a ligação química, os arranjos práticos de monitoramento, relato e verificação para a captura de carbono marítima permanecem pouco desenvolvidos, segundo a empresa. Ioulianou também alertou que os armadores não devem presumir que os benefícios reconhecidos no âmbito do EU ETS conferirão automaticamente vantagens de conformidade equivalentes no âmbito do FuelEU Maritime, que regula a intensidade de gases de efeito estufa da energia utilizada a bordo dos navios, e não as emissões absolutas. Ele observou que capturar carbono não é necessariamente o mesmo que entregar uma redução verificada de emissões, e que os armadores precisam de certeza sobre como as economias serão medidas, verificadas de forma independente e reconhecidas sob os regulamentos pertinentes. Sem essa clareza, disse ele, justificar o dispêndio de capital e os custos operacionais torna-se extremamente difícil. A EmissionLink entende que o período em que a IMO desenvolve seu marco de segurança deve ser aproveitado para avançar em paralelo com testes comerciais, procedimentos de verificação de emissões e infraestrutura portuária.

artigo.texto: Sierra Club Michigan launches online tracker of lawmakers’ and candidates’ data center stances LANSING, Mich. (News 10) - The Michigan chapter of the Sierra Club has launched an online “Data Center Position Tracker” that lists where state lawmakers and legislative candidates stand on data center policy. The Sierra Club said it’s asking whether lawmakers and candidates: - Support a temporary statewide moratorium on data centers - Would vote for strong regulations - Would vote to repeal the state’s data center tax incentives Marta Johnson of Sierra Club Michigan said the tracker is “intended to support advocacy and accountability efforts to accelerate data center legislative action.” Emily Woodcock, Michigan state director for Clean Water Action, a partner in the project, said the tracker is meant to put lawmakers on the record. “And so, this tool is a really important step that forces lawmakers to be on the record, stating something publicly that we can then hold them accountable to moving towards, you know, eventually having state laws that protect these communities.” Woodcock said. How the tracker works Each responding lawmaker or candidate is listed with a photo and an icon showing their stance on each of the three issues, with some entries including written statements. The Sierra Club says every legislator and candidate received at least two outreach attempts. The page also calls the list “crowdsourced” and invites people to ask their own lawmakers to write in with their position. Some responses are not yes or no Several officials and candidates offered answers that are more complicated than a simple “yes,” or “no.” Republican Sen. Michele Hoitenga said she would support a set of regulations, except for a requirement that data center projects use union labor, a regulation posed in the Sierra Club’s full questionnaire. “With regard to the question: Will you vote for permanent regulations to protect our water, energy grid, transparency, community benefits agreements, and require union labor, if put up for a vote? I would support all aspects of the bill with the exception of mandating union labor,” Hoitenga wrote. Democratic Sen. Jeff Irwin said he would vote to remove the sales tax reduction for large data center projects if protections for ratepayers and water use stay in law. He also wants to keep clean energy and efficiency standards that are in the same law. “I would vote to remove the sales tax reduction for large projects if we keep the provision protecting ratepayers by requiring MPSC to set rates such that residents are NOT subsidizing data centers and the provision requiring their water use to be provided and regulated by a municipal source. I wouldn’t want to lose local control and protections for water and ratepayers. We also have some clean energy and energy efficiency standards in the law granting sales tax exemptions, I would like to keep those standards as well,” Irwin wrote. Division on the data center issue Woodcock said Clean Water Action’s canvassers hear concerns “over affordability, what data centers will do to energy prices ... and what that could do to water across the state.” Johnson said the groups see a lack of transparency around data center projects, including nondisclosure agreements. Business groups see it differently. Mike Alaimo of the Michigan Chamber of Commerce told News 10 in September that hyperscale data centers provide a “massive opportunity” for the state, and that repealing incentives would show corporations that Michigan “is not open for business.” Concerns across party lines Woodcock said her group’s canvassers hear the same concern regardless of political affiliation. “It has been probably 20 years since there’s been an issue that has been like the number one issue for people that we talk to, regardless of location, political spectrum, background. This is something everyone is concerned with,” Woodcock said. “It is quite clear where the public stands on these issues. That is not the mystery. The mystery seems to be where their lawmakers stand,” said Nora Naughton with the Sierra Club. What’s next Johnson said the group expects to keep adding names. “We’re very optimistic that we’ll be able to continue to add lawmakers and decision makers onto this tracker. This is just our opening start for this effort,” she said. Bills on data center moratoriums, regulations and tax incentives have been introduced at the state Capitol this year, but so far, none have reached the Governor’s desk. artigo.texto: Meta toma uma dura do MPF A Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão do Ministério Público Federal (MPF) enviou à Meta uma lista de 12 recomendações para que adote "medidas urgentes" de transparência no período eleitoral para garantir "liberdade de expressão nas redes Facebook, Instagram, Threads e WhatsApp". Do site do MPF: A empresa têm prazo de 48 horas para responder se acatará as recomendações e para detalhar as providências que serão adotadas durante o segundo turno das eleições, além de 30 dias para apresentar relatório conclusivo. O MPF também apresentou à Justiça Federal de Porto Alegre (RS) ação civil pública para barrar bloqueios e restrições arbitrárias praticados pela Meta em redes sociais. A medida do MPF foi motivada pela representação das organizações Artigo 19, Conectas, Sleeping Giants e CTRL+Z, segundo as quais a Meta, em outubro e setembro deste ano, "aplicou número expressivo de sanções, como remoção de postagens, suspensão de perfis, restrição territorial e limitação de funcionalidade". [ATUALIZADO 22.out.2026 às 9h17] Em outra medida, o MPF também foi à Justiça para tentar forçar a Meta a restabelecer conteúdos e perfis derrubados arbitrariamente, em até 24 horas, sob pena de multa de R$500 mil por dia. De acordo com o jornal O Globo: Segundo o MPF, foram registrados mais de mil relatos de intervenções promovidas por plataformas digitais, especialmente a Meta e o X. A ação, no entanto, é direcionada apenas à Meta e à sua representante no Brasil. EIS A LISTA de recomendações propostas para os próximos cinco dias (até o segundo turno) enviada pela procuradoria do MPF. Os itens foram levemente editados pelo Núcleo para brevidade e clareza: - abstenha-se de remover publicações, suspender ou desativar contas, restringir territorialmente a visualização de conteúdos, reduzir alcance ou limitar funcionalidades sem fundamento jurídico ou contratual específico; - direcione recursos técnicos e recursos humanos para garantir prioritariamente as liberdades de opinião, de expressão e de manifestação, criando ajustes na moderação automática incidente sobre postagens com termos como “manifestação”, “convocação”, “ato público”, “passeata”, “marcha”, entre outros análogos, e submetendo-as, extraordinariamente, à revisão humana necessária; - aplique seus critérios de moderação de forma isonômica, sem distinção em razão da orientação política ou ideológica do conteúdo ou de seu autor; - direcione recursos técnicos e recursos humanos para para coibir o uso ilícito ou abusivo dos instrumentos de notificação submetendo necessariamente moderações decorrentes de denúncias em massa à revisão humana; - submeta à revisão humana a suspensão ou desativação de contas decorrentes de enquadramentos em infrações graves, como terrorismo e exploração sexual de crianças e adolescentes, sobretudo quando derivadas de reportes de outros usuários; - restabeleça imediatamente contas, publicações, alcance e funcionalidades quando reconhecido, por revisão humana, erro de moderação de conteúdo; - comunique, a cada usuário afetado, de forma individualizada, clara, acessível toda medida de moderação que lhe vier a ser imposta, inclusive a decorrente de sistema automatizado, informando a natureza e a duração da medida, a natureza da infração atribuída, a regra aplicada, os elementos que justificaram o enquadramento, a origem da decisão e os meios e prazos de contestação, e valendo-se, extraordinariamente, do recurso denominado “Megafone”, já empregado pela empresa, que permitiria informar aos usuários, em posição destacada de seus feed, quando forem alvo de uma dada restrição, sem necessidade de recorrerem ao Painel de Status da Conta - de modo a melhor cumprir com os deveres de transparência aqui delineados; - reconheça (no prazo máximo de 02 dias), valendo-se do mesmo recurso “Megafone” ou de outro análogo, as falhas de moderação de conteúdo apontadas pelo Comitê de Supervisão, e formule pedido público de desculpas; - assegure, em posição destacada do feed de cada usuário, um link de fácil acesso aos procedimentos de contestação gratuita para todas as modalidades de restrição; - comprometa-se (no prazo máximo de 03 dias) com a contratação de uma auditoria independente para analisar os algoritmos de moderação utilizados nas plataformas controladas pela Meta ao longo dos últimos dois meses; - comprometa-se (no prazo máximo de 03 dias), com a elaboração, sugerida pelo Comitê de Supervisão da Meta, de um arcabouço de métricas para avaliar os esforços da empresa em favor da integridade das eleições no Brasil, indo além das meras referências, hoje realizadas, a dados agregados de anúncios veiculados ou de número contas removidas; - preserve os registros técnicos, documentos e informações sobre os episódios, incluídas as decisões de moderação, seus fundamentos, as notificações recebidas e os pedidos de revisão, observados os limites legais de proteção de dados pessoais e de sigilo das comunicações. [ATUALIZAÇÃO 22.out.2026 às 9h16] A Meta informou que não irá comentar a um pedido de comentários feito pelo Núcleo por email. >> Íntegra do documento do MPF

artigo.texto: Oriente Médio é a região mais barata para construir data centers com a alta da demanda por IA O Oriente Médio ocupa a posição de região mais barata do mundo para a construção de data centers e, portanto, está bem posicionado para se beneficiar da migração para projetos de inteligência artificial em grande escala, segundo pesquisa da Turner & Townsend, empresa global de gestão de programas. O Data Centre Construction Index da companhia, agora em sua décima edição, compara custos de construção com base em mais de 500 projetos em andamento ou concluídos recentemente em 62 mercados, com o apoio de uma pesquisa com mais de 400 especialistas do setor. O estudo coloca a média do Oriente Médio em US$ 9,93 por watt, abaixo da Europa, com US$ 12,76, da Ásia, com US$ 12,10, e da América do Norte, com US$ 12,06. Três mercados do Oriente Médio aparecem entre as 62 localidades cobertas: a Arábia Saudita, com US$ 10,80, em 40º lugar; o Catar, com US$ 9,80, em 53º; e os Emirados Árabes Unidos, com US$ 9,20, em 58º. Alan Coary, diretor e responsável pela área de data centers no Oriente Médio da Turner & Townsend, atribuiu a posição da região a custos de construção e de energia comparativamente baixos, aliados a forte apoio governamental à infraestrutura de IA. Ele citou a iniciativa HUMAIN, da Arábia Saudita, e o investimento contínuo dos Emirados Árabes Unidos em IA e no desenvolvimento de data centers de hiperescala por meio da G42 e da Khazna como fatores que remodelam a capacidade computacional da região e sustentam sua ambição de ser um polo de IA competitivo globalmente, refletindo uma tendência mais ampla de IA soberana e de programas de infraestrutura digital apoiados por governos. No mundo, os custos de construção de data centers continuaram a subir em 2026, à medida que a demanda por capacidade computacional de IA e por projetos de grande escala superou a oferta de terrenos com energia disponível e de mão de obra qualificada. Embora a inflação global de custos tenha mostrado alguma estabilização em 2026, custos e riscos de construção estruturalmente mais altos vêm sendo cada vez mais precificados nos contratos, enquanto a escassez crescente de qualificação aumenta a pressão sobre os custos de mão de obra. A alta dos custos é cada vez mais impulsionada pela escala crescente das obras, sobretudo das instalações de IA, que exigem abordagens alternativas de entrega, especialistas técnicos e novos modelos de equilíbrio de riscos para aliviar a capacidade sobrecarregada e acelerar os cronogramas. Entre os entrevistados, 52% esperam que a maior parte de seus projetos de 2027 sejam data centers que atendam a cargas de trabalho de IA. Além disso, 52% relataram aumentos de custos acima de 6% em 2026, e cerca de 20% citaram inflação acima de 15%. Para 2027, 28% dos entrevistados globais esperam inflação entre 1% e 5%, o que indica continuidade do arrefecimento da pressão de custos, e 57% esperam inflação abaixo de 15%. A energia foi apontada como um dos principais obstáculos à entrega bem-sucedida por 56% dos entrevistados, com 52% relatando que as conexões à rede elétrica costumam levar de um a dois anos e 32% relatando prazos superiores a dois anos. As localidades mais caras do índice foram Tóquio, com US$ 18,28; Osaka, com US$ 17,15; Zurique, com US$ 15,93; Singapura, com US$ 15,39; e o Vale do Silício, com US$ 15,01. O Japão ocupa o primeiro lugar, enquanto 17 mercados europeus e 13 norte-americanos compõem quase metade da tabela principal, refletindo a contínua dominância dessas regiões. Cerca de metade de todos os data centers do mundo está na América do Norte, e um quarto, na Europa. As localidades mais baratas foram Xangai, com US$ 5,79; Mumbai, com US$ 6,83; Cidade de Ho Chi Minh, com US$ 8,32; Bogotá, com US$ 9,13; e os Emirados Árabes Unidos, com US$ 9,20. Esses mercados emergentes oferecem mão de obra mais barata e maior acesso a ela. Paul Barry, responsável pelo índice de custos de construção na Turner & Townsend, disse que o setor se transformou ao longo da década desde a primeira publicação do índice, com o investimento de capital em data centers agora em US$ 800 bilhões por ano e expectativa de chegar a US$ 1,8 trilhão até 2050. Ele afirmou que a rápida demanda da IA por capacidade computacional, combinada à adoção da nuvem e à importância crescente dos dados e da capacidade soberana, impulsiona investimentos e desenvolvimento em escala sem precedentes e remodela o cenário da construção. Ele também observou que o aumento dos custos de materiais e de mão de obra continua a criar desafios em todo o mundo, enquanto o acesso a energia, a equipamentos especializados e a qualificação segue como gargalo. Os data centers enfrentam escrutínio crescente, o que torna o consentimento político e das comunidades essencial para a entrega, e a demanda impulsionada pela IA por energia em nível de gigawatt e por resfriamento líquido para maiores densidades de rack alimenta projetos de maior escala, enquanto a escassez de mão de obra qualificada e os maiores riscos na entrega de projetos mais complexos impõem um prêmio de custo.

artigo.texto: MaxVolt Energy Showcases Energy Storage and EV Battery Portfolio at REI Expo 2026 MaxVolt Energy presented its rack-type energy storage systems, lithium inverter batteries and EV battery packs on the opening day of REI Expo 2026. October 26, 2026. By News Bureau MaxVolt Energy Industries showcased its energy storage and electric mobility battery portfolio on the opening day of the 19th edition of the Renewable Energy India Expo (REI Expo) 2026 in Greater Noida. The company presented its rack-type ESS from 4.8 kWh to 60 kWh for homes, solar installations and Commercial and Industrial (C&I) sites, with battery life of up to 10 years. Alongside these were lithium inverter batteries, MaxVolt’s storage inverters, solar batteries and lithium battery packs for electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers. Together they showcased MaxVolt’s range across both renewable storage and electric mobility. Mukesh Gupta, Co-Founder and Chief Marketing Officer, MaxVolt Energy Industries, said, “REI Expo is where the people building India’s renewable future come looking for partners they can rely on. Our message this year is clear: MaxVolt makes storage for every scale, from a home to a factory floor, alongside the EV batteries our partners already know us for. Our dealers and OEM partners have taken us to 22 states. The conversations at our stall, with installers, EPC firms and distributors, tell us the market is ready to move from lead-acid to lithium, and we are ready to meet it.” REI Expo brings India’s solar and storage ecosystem under one roof, and this year storage is central to that conversation. As solar capacity grows, battery storage is what makes renewable power usable round the clock. The Central Electricity Authority projects India will need about 208 GWh of battery storage by 2029-30. MaxVolt’s showcase answers that need directly: storage that works with solar, from a single home to a factory floor. Bhuvneshwar Pal Singh, Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer, MaxVolt Energy Industries Limited, added, “FY26 gave us a strong base. As we move through the second half of FY27, our focus is disciplined, profitable growth: making full use of our Duhai capacity, deepening our dealer and OEM network, and building Aligarh in phases so that new capacity comes up in step with demand. Energy storage is a growing part of that plan, and we expect it to play a larger role in our business in the years ahead.” The company has been manufacturing since 2019 and now runs a 2.5 GWh plant at Duhai, Ghaziabad. The company reported FY26 revenue of INR 296.8 crore, up 176 percent year on year, with profit after tax of INR 24.4 crore. Its network covers 950 plus dealers and 170 plus OEM partners across 22 states. In September 2026, MaxVolt held the bhoomi poojan for a planned 10 GWh plant at Khyamai Industrial Estate, Aligarh. The plant represents an investment of INR 700 crore and will be built in two phases of 5 GWh each. When complete, it will take the company’s total capacity to 12.5 GWh and is expected to create 1,500 to 2,000 direct jobs. The plant is designed to meet growing demand across all of MaxVolt’s segments, including dedicated lines for OEM partners. The company’s roadmap also includes a planned entry into four-wheeler EV batteries and continued Battery Management System (BMS) research with IIT Roorkee. Through its recycling subsidiary, MaxVolt ReEarth, the company is building a circular approach to the batteries it makes. please contact: contact@energetica-india.net.

artigo.texto: MINERAL EXPLORADO NA BAHIA DEVE GANHAR FORÇA COM IA E DATA CENTERS A expansão da inteligência artificial (IA) e dos data centers pode ampliar a demanda por vanádio produzido na Bahia, impulsionada pela necessidade de tecnologias de armazenamento de energia em larga escala. O mineral é utilizado na fabricação de baterias de fluxo de vanádio, que podem armazenar eletricidade por longos períodos e atender a instalações que exigem fornecimento contínuo de energia. A Bahia tem participação relevante no setor mineral nacional. O estado produz vanádio e urânio e responde pela extração de 47 das 93 tipologias minerais existentes no Brasil. A mineradora canadense Largo opera a mina Maracás Menchen, na Bahia, considerada uma das principais operações de vanádio do mundo. Além de liderar a produção de vanádio e urânio, o estado é responsável por produzir 47 das 93 tipologias minerais existentes no Brasil. Tradicionalmente, o vanádio é empregado na fabricação de aços de alta resistência e ligas metálicas especiais. Nos últimos anos, o mineral também ganhou espaço nas discussões sobre tecnologias de armazenamento de energia, especialmente diante da expansão das fontes renováveis e do aumento do consumo de eletricidade por instalações digitais. Eletricidade prolongada Diferentemente das baterias convencionais de íons de lítio, essa tecnologia armazena energia em soluções líquidas que contêm vanádio. Os líquidos circulam entre tanques e células eletroquímicas, permitindo o armazenamento de grandes volumes de eletricidade por períodos prolongados. Entre as características das baterias de fluxo estão a possibilidade de armazenamento por várias horas, a longa vida útil e o menor risco de incêndio em comparação com algumas tecnologias convencionais. Essas características podem tornar o sistema uma alternativa para aplicações industriais, redes elétricas e data centers, que precisam manter servidores e equipamentos de processamento em funcionamento contínuo. O avanço da inteligência artificial amplia a demanda por capacidade computacional e, consequentemente, por infraestrutura elétrica. Nesse cenário, soluções de armazenamento podem contribuir para a gestão do fornecimento de energia e para a estabilidade das redes. Mercado brasileiro de data centers Segundo a consultoria imobiliária JLL, o mercado brasileiro de data centers deve dobrar de tamanho até 2030. No primeiro semestre de 2026, o Brasil registrou 706 megawatts (MW) de capacidade instalada no segmento, de acordo com os dados apresentados no levantamento. O volume representa um crescimento superior a seis vezes em relação a 2012, equivalente a uma taxa composta de crescimento anual de 15%. A expansão dos centros de processamento de dados exige investimentos em geração, transmissão e sistemas de reserva de energia. Essa necessidade pode abrir espaço para tecnologias de armazenamento de longa duração, entre elas as baterias de fluxo de vanádio. Para a Largo, a ampliação desse mercado representa uma possibilidade de diversificação da demanda pelo mineral, atualmente utilizado sobretudo pela indústria siderúrgica. A concretização dessa oportunidade, porém, depende da evolução da adoção da tecnologia e dos investimentos em infraestrutura energética. Setores de defesa e aeroespacial Além das aplicações no armazenamento de eletricidade, o vanádio é utilizado na produção de aços de alta resistência e ligas metálicas destinadas a setores como defesa e indústria aeroespacial. A demanda norte-americana também integra a estratégia comercial da Largo. Em julho, a mineradora recebeu um aporte de US$ 60,1 milhões para fornecer pentóxido de vanádio de alta pureza aos Estados Unidos, com entregas previstas até janeiro de 2030. A empresa é fornecedora da Agência de Logística de Defesa dos Estados Unidos (DLA). Segundo a companhia canadense, o relacionamento comercial com os Estados Unidos também está associado ao interesse de países ocidentais em reduzir a dependência de fornecedores como China e Rússia. *Com informações do Portal A Tarde.

artigo.texto: Dubuque County targets traffic, emergency strain as data center debate looms over election DUBUQUE, Iowa (KCRG) - Dubuque County leaders want to make sure developers, not local taxpayers, pay for busy roads and strained emergency services if large data centers break ground in the area. During a dedicated work session Monday, the Dubuque County Board of Supervisors questioned local law enforcement to determine how narrow secondary roads and emergency crews would survive years of industrial construction. The discussions come as the county nears the November election, with Supervisor Ann McDonough not seeking re-election at the end of her term and incumbent Wayne Kenniker on the ballot. Dubuque County is several months into a one-year moratorium on large-scale facilities, giving officials until next July to craft a binding regulatory ordinance. Sheriff Joe Kennedy told supervisors his review of other Iowa communities with active data centers showed that once operating, the facilities rarely require police assistance. “Once the construction is complete, there’s a limited number of people that actually work inside the facilities,” Kennedy said. “The actual issues that they have on site once the thing’s operational are pretty minimal.” The disruption, Kennedy noted, comes during the building process, when hundreds of workers, heavy machinery, and constant material deliveries descend onto two-lane county routes like Sundown Road. “When it comes to the traffic, it’s really going to depend on what the scope of the project is,” Kennedy said. “At the entrances we’re probably going to have an increased number of rear-end accidents and things like that.” To prevent public deputies from being pulled from regular patrols, Kennedy urged supervisors to write rules requiring developers to pay for off-duty law enforcement to direct traffic. “Obviously, we have limited resources, so it’s not like we can just go down there and send our people down there all day on duty and tie them up all day with that,” Kennedy said. “I think that it’s a small cost for these data center companies to ensure that they have safe operations going in and out of there.” That friction on rural roadways is already hitting home for neighbors. During public comments, resident Mary Beth Decker explained that harvest traffic already makes walking along rural routes a hazard. “I had to give that up because the semis, the tractors, and things going down there became too dangerous,” Decker said. “I had to make a different route...especially during harvest time.” McDonough pointed out that draft proposals limiting construction to daytime hours and weekdays will compress traffic into tight windows, creating logistical headaches. “There’s not night shifts to this for construction. And there’s no weekend construction, at least that’s the draft. So it’s going to be a resource issue,” McDonough said. She stressed that dropping a massive campus into a rural area demands intensive preparation before a shovel moves. “This isn’t like somebody gives you a flyer and says they’re going to be open on Monday,” McDonough said. “There’s close coordinated communication about how something this big would roll.” Monday’s focus on roads adds to months of mounting testimony at the courthouse. Last month, public health officials urged supervisors to adopt strict decibel caps, warning that continuous noise from cooling systems and server fans causes chronic stress, elevated blood pressure, and sleep disruption. Residents have also raised concerns over local landfill capacity, asking whether regional sites could handle large volumes of demolition and electronic waste. McDonough’s decision not to seek re-election means the county will swear in at least one new supervisor in January as the board continues working toward a final ordinance.
